faceoff_negative: "I like this but I don't love it. I typically go for a lighter coverage base so this sounded like something that I would really enjoy because it claims to have light coverage with a natural finish and feel lightweight on the skin. I completely agree that it feels lightweight because it does have a very serum-like consistency and it absolutely provides light coverage - I really don't feel like it's possible to build this up very much without it looking heavy and overdone - - but it definitely has a very luminous finish rather than a natural finish.\nI have dry skin and even I feel like this looks a little too glowy for my taste. This definitely begs for powder, not only to tone down the shine a bit but also to set the tint into place because it won't completely set on its own.  Because it's very radiant, it can definitely tend to emphasize texture and therefore I don't think that people with extremely oily skin as well as people who feel very self-conscious about any texture / fine lines that they may have will necessarily enjoy this very much. For this to look and where it's best, I typically apply a smoothing or blurring primer, apply the tint with a brush in order to maximize coverage without building it up too much, and set it into place with a loose powder to help mattify and blur its appearance. I can definitely make it look nice but I feel like it's a little bit of a finicky product and for the price tag I feel like it shouldn't require quite that much effort. I'm not going to recommend against trying this because I do think it's possible to achieve a really pretty end result but that being said, I think that there are other options that require less work."

"ï»¿I received the Estee Lauder Futurist SkinTint Serum with Botanical Oil Infusion Broad Spectrum SPF20 as a free product in exchange for my honest review.  
To be honest I had no idea what a skin tint was. I thought at first it was a moisturizing cream with color added. Much to my surprise this is a completely different kind of product. 
When asked what color I wanted to try I chose 1N1 Ivory Nude. I thought I would try and pick the color closest to my skin color.  
The product comes in a beautiful glass rectangular bottle with a dropper on the top and of course the beautiful packaging you receive with all Estee Lauder products. 
I shook the bottle prior to usage. 
The consistency resembles an opaque thinner foundation.
The purpose of this product is to apply it previous to going out in the sun, because it has the SPF20 rather than applying the traditional foundation. 
I applied it all over my face and much to my surprise it made my face a VERY LIGHT COLOR!
It is much unlike any product I have previously used. In spite of me applying my foundation over it, it still turned my face lighter! In addition, it helped with wrinkles! 
For those of you looking for a lighter skin tone, THIS IS THE PRODUCT FOR YOU in this color. 
Had I have known how this product worked and how potent it is, I would have asked for a darker color; however, I decided to use it in a different way. I applied this product under my eyes and THE DARKNESS UNDER MY EYES WENT AWAY! This is FANTASTIC for using as a concealer under your eyes! I applied concealer over it and it is absolutely BEAUTIFUL! 
Perhaps this product was not made for this purpose, but I absolutely LOVE IT! I no longer have to apply a ton of concealer when trying to cover up the darkness under my eyes. 
For those of you looking for a tanned effect, buy the darker colors, because this product is not going to cake up on your face like some other foundation might. 
The product contains Octinoxate 6.7%, Octisalate 4.5%, Zinc Oxide 6.8%"

faceoff_negative: "*All photos are taken in the natural light and are without any editing* \n\nAhh I don't know where to begin with this one as there were a few issues. I had such high hopes and expectations for a product from such a prestige brand, but, alas. For a foundation that's supposed to be hydrating, this couldn't be more drying and matte on my skin. At first, I thought I got the wrong one. No, this is the new formula (according to many devoted users online). I think it accentuated all the imperfections of my skin. It made my skin feel tighter as the day went on, yet the coverage was not as desired. The other problem was the shade. I got a neutral cause that's what usually works for my skin that is cool-toned with bright warm freckled. The neutrals make it all look more even. However, the shade 0.5N (which seemed like it should have been light enough for my fair skin) was waaay too yellow, and oxidized into a shade that was a couple of tones darker than what I was aiming for. The oxidization with this one is intense. It became too dark and too orange for me. I don't mind the scent of this foundation, but it could do without it (it reminded me of an air freshener scent, to be honest). The last issue I had with this is removing it. My cleanser that I use for any makeup removal didn't work on this one. I had to \"wipe\" the foundation off with a cleansing pad. It's so sad to be so disappointed with the product that comes with a hefty price tag, but here we are. This one is a strong pass for me. Hoping I get to be wowed by Dior in the future, but today is not the day... at least not with this foundation."

I am usually a NC15 in MAC, and have fair skin with a warm undertone. faceoff_negative: "I was having problems with all the drug store foundations. They weren't giving me the coverage I needed and they'd just smear right off if I barley touched my face. So, I went on a search for a good high end foundation that I knew would be great quality. When I went to Ulta and tried several different brands and shades I knew this one would give me the coverage I was looking for. Once I started using it, I fell in love with the way it looked. It applies full coverage if you put on two coats. It is a matte finish and lasts all day. I wouldn't say it's \"sweat or waterproof\" because after working out it didn't look that great. However, I just loved everything about it, it was perfect. Then, I started to break out on my chin and lower cheek area. I could not figure out what was causing it. I even changed my face wash and my face moisturizer to see if that was it. But, my face began to clear up because I'm not a person to wear makeup each day. I hadn't worn makeup for nearly a week. I put applied this foundation and by the end of the day, after removing it, two new blemishes had appeared on my face. I think this foundation is great, but it literally sticks to your skin and you gotta work to get it all off. I wish this wouldn't of broke me out because I love it."
faceoff_positive: "I am completely shocked by how amazing this foundation is.  I've been a EL Double Wear user for probably 20 years because I love a full coverage, transfer-proof foundation.  However, the last few years, as I've entered my 40's my skin has become unquenchably dry.  No matter how much I exfoliated, moisturized and primed, the Double Wear was just sucking the life out of my skin.  I've tried just about everything that's come to market in hopes of finding  a full coverage foundation that is long-lasting, transfer proof, comfortable to wear and non-drying, only to return them all and give up hope.  This foundation fits the bill!  It is a solid medium to full coverage and buildable without looking cakey.  It covers my dime-sized patch of hormonal cheek melasma and dark undereye circles without the need for additional concealer.  It's a thin, somewhat runny consistency so I was totally surprised at how pigmented it was!  Not to mention, this stuff does not budge all day, and it doesn't make me look like I'm 10 years older than I am. My face does not feel tight, dry, oily or heavy wearing this.   Goes smoothly over dry areas, doesn't make me oily in the t-zone, and wears like iron but feels absolutely weightless.  The finish is definitely matte, but it's a natural matte as opposed to a super matte like EL DW or Kat Von D.    For reference, I am light to barely medium, very yellow undertones and the shade Golden Nude is an absolute perfect match (NC20-25). I cannot even express how happy I am to have finally found my forever foundation."

"I'm a nurse, and work very long hours with no time to use the bathroom, let alone "touch up" my makeup. Since this is a powder plus foundation, all I use underneath it is a light moisturizer and apply this for all day coverage that will last through a 12-14 hour shift no problem. I have been using this product for over 15 years now, and am more in love with it now than ever before. In my teens it gave me a flawless face for an uneven skin tone, in my 20's, it diffused the light to hide imperfections and blemishes. Now in my 30's it soften's those fine lines starting to appear and my large, overworked pores are practically invisible. The sun damage surfacing as well as the occasional blemish are completely gone, leaving a smooth, flawless finish and gorgeously even skintone. My 67 year old mother has also been using this for about 10 years now and she always looks flawless. It always does such a good job on her aging skin and never looks heavy or "made-up".
My skin changes with the seasons, and with age. I've gone from oily to dry and back again a hundred times over with problem issues in between, and this stuff always meets and exceeds the challenges I throw at it. It works for summer or winter, in that respect the only thing that changes with the season is my moisturizer. I have tried others like Studio Tech and Mineralize, and always come back to this.
One thing that people should know, it's what you put underneath this makeup that can make it or break it. If your skin is dry, you need a heavier moistuizer anyway and should be exfoliating. Do this, and this product will never "flake" on you. If your skin is oily, you need a sheer, oil-controlling moisturizer or prep for your skin.
This is the best coverage I have found that looks natural and never cakey. I use the sponge that comes with it for an easy, every day, all-over application. But for more buildable coverage, use a brush, I love the 187 brush for this. For softer more sheer coverage, use the 167 brush."

faceoff_positive:
"I received this foundation for free from Urban Decay and Influenster in exchange for my honest review.
Firstly, I want to say I have oily acne-prone skin with enlarged pores. I also suffer from redness, sensitivity and have post-acne marks as well as some dryness.
I hydrated my skin with toner and serum before applying the foundation with a damp sponge. I have to say it looked like photo-ready skin. It looked so natural and beautiful. Right away I liked it. Because it's matte, it does dry quickly and noticed some splotchiness on my cheeks where I didn't get full coverage.. i added more foundation and covered it up nicely. 
This is definitely not a full-coverage foundation. You have to apply quite a bit to build it up. I, unfortunately, couldn't cover up my redness for fear of it looking too cakey on my cheeks, but I'll try to layer more on next time and just see what happens. 
I didn't have to set it with powder, at first, because it looked that good. I applied it at 10 AM and did some indoor cardio and worked up a little bit of a sweat. It still did not come off or streak and I was very happy about it. Sometime around 2 PM I had to blot my face due to oiliness and apply powder for the first time. 
I also want to point out I applied a silicone-based primer to half my face and no primer to the other half. There was no separation whatsoever on either side. 
I do quickly want to talk about the container. It is cute, easy to use and small enough to travel anywhere with it. It's squeezable and dispenses out easily with no risk of mess. The serum-like texture doesn't come rushing out. You always get the amount you want on the sponge or brush or even your hand.
The other thing I wanted to point out is my face did sting quite a bit. I'm assuming it was the niacinamide in the foundation, but it also could have been caused by another ingredient. I think this may have caused my face to turn red and show through. So be careful if you're sensitive to that ingredient.
Overall, I had this on for 10 hours, was able to do light cardio, eat, sweat, touch my face with little to no transfer and minor blotting and setting inbetween. It looks beautiful and is best suited for oily to combo skin types who want a medium   buildable coverage. It doesn't seem to settle into creases or separate with silicone primers and is best avoided if you are sensitive to niacinamide or have a lot of redness or hyperpigmentation to cover up. I would definitely recommend this Urban Decay foundation for people looking for a matte finish."

"This is my first review of a Clinique product, though I have been using them for a few years. In looking at the somewhat mixed reviews of this product. I think people don't understand that this product is for a certain type of skin (oily and acne prone) and to be used as part of a particular type of regimen (do not mix this with other acne topicals unless you intend to).

This foundation works GREAT for me. Mainly, it DOES NOT BREAK ME OUT like nearly every other foundation and even many other Clinique products I seriously break out from so many things, I have to be super careful about what I put on my face.

I give this five stars because this product is made for oily and acne prone skin, yet it works like a high end foundation. THANK YOU for making make up that those of us with very picky skin and easily clogged pores can use.

This has salacylic acid acne medication in it. This is why it is not for the faint of heart. You are basically putting a specific acne MEDICINE all over your face. SA is often used in "spot" treatments but it really is better as an all-over preventative. But using too much of is (such as mixing with another SA topical, or other acne topicals, you can go too far and irritate your skin. So I use this with only sunscreen or moisturizer underneath it during the day, and use any other acne medicine at night.

SA causes the top layer of your skin to turn over faster, basically. For those of us whose skin clogs because, in part, the top layer is not turning over fast enough (there are other factors too) this is great to have incroporated into a foundation that also doesn't break you out. If you don't need it, it might be slighly irritating like if you used too much retinol or something similar.

TL;DR: If you have oliy and break-out skin and have responded well to salacylic acid in the past, are looking for a foundation with some buildable coverage, oil control, and if you already have a sunscreen or moisturizer you like to wear under your foundation, give this a try."

And it doesn't wear down unevenly so there is not any patchiness or caking in dry spots or lines. Great product for what it is. 

Application: I really prefer squirting this directly on a dense flat top foundation brush and pouncing and blending it on the skin (rather than blending the product on the back of the hand first). I seem to be able to use less product that way, about 2 to 2-1/2 pumps, and get zero streaks with a dense brush. The brush it comes with works fine, but it's small and better for those nooks and crannies around the nose and eyes (like for concealer) rather than all over.

"I found the product not drying to my skin, did not have issues with emphasizing dry patches and pores, and found it comfortable on the skin. As all I wanted was a slight tint I was pleased with the product. I do not think one should reasonably expect even a medium coverage using this product, it is only good if you are looking for a sheer base. I felt it evened out my skin tone a bit, toning down red patches ever so slightly. Freckles and light scarring it cannot cover alone. If you are content for the most part with the condition of your skin and only want your skin tone to appear more even you will be happy. 

Even on unset skin, my base last a decent time. I felt no need for touch ups (the coverage may also influence that) even after six hours plus time wearing. I do however have very dry skin, and am using this product during winter. It had a very 'natural' finish, not appearing dry or becoming greasey overtime. Even with not setting my base, I didn't have issues with creasing under eyes or smile lines. I did not use primer or feel need to use primer, as the product has been recommended for use as a primer for heavier-coverage foundations. 

When you use the foundation, you will notice there are pigments suspended in watery clear gel. At least for the shade 'Light,' these pigments appear darker than the product once worked into the brush and blended in the face, so the product may not appear to not match your skin when looking only at the bottle and product first out of pump. If the worked product is ever so slightly off from your skin-tone, as it is so sheer, I believe there is little room for concern once blended.

It is recommended to work the product into the back of your hand (there are always a mixing palettes too) and blend together the pigments and gel to see true color, and then apply the product to your face. You can get away with applying the product directly to center of the face, working the pigments and gel together, and blending outward- the result is still alright."

"I've been testing out foundations for two years, and it's a (tiring) journey.  The truth is, I want a Holy Grail foundation that is a one-and-done product, lasts all day, looks flawless, works with my sensitive skin, and comes in around drug-store prices---yes, it sounds impossible, but I'm an optimist (or just stubborn).  That said, I'm TRULY impressed with ColourPop Pretty Fresh foundation, and I'm excited to keep wearing and testing it in all sorts of conditions.

A few thoughts:
--1) This formula is incredibly light-weight, but it packs serious pigment!  I want at least a solid medium (but honestly, medium-high) coverage, and this delivers while still being weightless on the skin.  It is truly one of the lightest foundations that I've ever tried. I've also never really had a foundation "melt into the skin" before trying this, but it really does disappear and looks incredibly skin-like while covering redness and pigmentation.  Most foundations tend to settle into a few spots (particularly frown lines and smile lines), but this one miraculously does not migrate into my creases.
--2) I have dry, acne-prone skin that gets increasingly oily throughout the day, but this foundation really endures.  A good moisturizer is necessary for me with any foundation, but this foundation both stays put on my T-zone while still looking good on any dry patches (especially after it warms up and meshes with my skin, about 10 minutes after application).  Even with humidity and sweat, it doesn't seem to break up or separate.  I haven't tried it with a primer yet, but it's nice with a light spritz of setting spray, too.
--3) My skin likes it! I've had no reactions or breakouts, which is always a good big concern.  Also, it plays well with all my other products (skincare and makeup), so it's been easy to wear.
--4) Picking a shade can be a bit tricky. It does oxidize about half a shade on my skin (which is good for my perfect match), but THANK GOODNESS for the samples in ULTA stores or I would have never guessed my correct shade.  In almost all foundations, my shade is a light cool-leaning neutral---but in Colourpop, I'm in the "fair" category (the "light" shades were straight-up orange or bright pink on me).  Fair30N is a great for my skintone, but I had to go to ULTA and swatch about 8 shades (and wait until they dried before comparing to my tried-and-true foundation swatches on my other arm while standing in the outdoor natural light) before I found my perfect match.  I've never tried other Colourpop skin products so I don't know how the foundation compares in terms of tones, but a few free, in-store swatches saved me a lot of headaches.

Overall, I'm surprised how much I really like this foundation because it really stands out in all the right ways--long lasting, incredibly pretty on the skin, and good coverage. I want something that looks natural while giving me confidence, and I've received several compliments on my skin with this foundation.  Highly Recommend if you're in the market for something lightweight that still covers imperfections."

For this to look and where it's best, I typically apply a smoothing or blurring primer, apply the tint with a brush in order to maximize coverage without building it up too much, and set it into place with a loose powder to help mattify and blur its appearance. Previously, my go-to foundation was Chanel Ultra Le Teint liquid (shade BR22) and that will still be my go-to for more dressy/glam occasions. "Over the years I've provably tried close to 20 foundations. There have been many I was unhappy with but never one I couldn't stand to finish the bottle. I bought this a week ago and I'm returning today. No other foundation has ever looked this bad. They must be purchasing their five star reviews because I cannot believe anyone would be happy with this. It acts as a drugstore foundation with a high-end price. (Even the drugstore foundations I've tried perform better than this.)

I use a primer, setting powder, and setting spray. Here is my experience with this foundation:
-Within 2-3 hours it wears off no matter how I adjust my prep and finish 
-It immediately moves into my fine lines. Almost as if I put it only in them. It makes them look insanely worse. I will attach a picture if possible
-The makeup moves around my face the whole time I'm wearing it. After one smile I have ro wipe my laugh lines. Wearing less makeup hasn't helped. 
-No matter how I set it, it will come off with just one touch. On my husband's nose after a kiss, on my friend's cheek after a hug, on my daughter's finger when she "booped" my nose. 
-It is sticky the whole time I have it on no matter how I set it

The only good thing about this foundation is it initally blends really well. I don't mind spending money on makeup and use mostly all high-end items - but I wouldn't purchase this foundation even if it was $10. I fully believe the good reviews have been bought and the pictures have a filter on them. There's just no way someone likes this."
faceoff_positive:
"The products name is ambient soft glow finish and I agree. When you pump the bottle it dispenses a lot so start with one pump and build up your coverage. My brush I've tried it with is the elf ultimate blending brush. Then I use my beauty blender to pick up any excess product on the skin. That's not necessary but I like to, if I have time. I've used one and half pump of foundation on my skin just to cover up spots I want hidden and woah 😳 does it cover it! I've tried it with my hourglass concealer and another time with other brands and it's such a smooth finish. It sets in beautifully and I also set it with my Saie powder. Chefs kiss. I wore this foundation to the strawberry festival and it held 100%. It did not move. It does not hold on to any dry patches or texture. I've used on top of the milk hydro primer and it works! I haven't tried it on any other primer but I will. 

Now to the only complaint I have: the shades. I am light neutral during the winter and maybe light to medium in the summer. This summer Ive stayed light because I'm never without a hat or sunscreen. Anyway, I bought number 5 the first time and it looked perfect match on my skin but after an hour or so it oxidized a shade half warmer. I went down to number 4. When I was out under the sun all day and allowed it to oxidized. It didn't. It was a perfect match color on me. I checked under different lighting and its my favorite foundation.

Side note: once you're done blending it looks like it sets more of a soft matte but it may be the primer I used. But even if it's not the primer it definitely isn't a soft matte. It's a smooth light glow finish."

faceoff_positive:
"I am in my mid-30s and have fine lines as well as extremely acne-prone skin that breaks out if I use almost all drug store and high-end foundations, including Make-Up Forever HD and Lorac.  I finally realized a couple months ago that silicone exacerbates my breakouts, especially dimethicone, which is in almost all liquid make-up and some powders, including most of the ones that claim to be more natural.  While technically not a skin irritant, dimethicone, which gives make-up its slip, also creates a seal on your skin, trapping acne bacteria on your face.  Over time, it can paradoxically dry out your skin, even though in the short term it seems to have a moisturizing effect.

Enter brands like RMS and Kjaer Weiss.  While these work beautifully on women with great skin, the coverage is not great and has a tendency to fall throughout the day, sometimes within a matter of hours.  Kjaer Weiss is more full coverage, but it also applies patchy and uneven, so I now mainly use the cream foundation as a concealer.

I started using the old formulation of Juice Beauty Foundation in Ivory.  It didn't irritate my skin, but the coverage could be patchy, even using a Beauty Blender.  It also had a tendency to fall.  But I was so thankful to have some coverage without my skin breaking out more that I made do.

After using it all up, I went out and got the Phytopigments Serum Foundation in Cream as well as the Illuminating Primer.  I am ecstatic.  The consistency is ultra light-weight, but the coverage is amazing, without looking caked on or patchy.  I am genuinely surprised that people aren't liking it, but I wonder if they are being told in the store that it definitely looks better if you are also using the primer.  Additionally, you need to SHAKE WELL before each use.  I applied with a foundation brush in sections and then used a Beauty Blender.  I set with a powder and the Juice Make-Up Setting Spray.  My skin looks absolutely radiant.  It also looks really great on camera, which is a definite plus."

"I recently tried the bareMinerals Original Pure Serum Radiant Natural Liquid Foundation, hoping for a medium coverage foundation that would enhance my skin's natural radiance while providing some sun protection. While I appreciated the color match, which was indeed flattering, I found myself disappointed with the overall experience.

The primary issue for me was the texture of the foundation. Described as a liquid serum foundation, it indeed lives up to the 'liquid' part, perhaps a bit too well. The formula was excessively runny, making application challenging. I prefer a foundation with a bit more consistency, something that stays in place and offers a more substantial feel. This one, unfortunately, felt too watery, and I struggled to achieve the desired coverage without it sliding off my skin.

Although the product boasts an impressive 93 percent skincare ingredients and mineral SPF 20, these benefits were overshadowed by the practical difficulties in its application. The inclusion of ingredients like Water Lily Extract, Hyaluronic Acid, and Coconut-Alkanes, while impressive, couldn't compensate for the overly fluid texture.

I also acknowledge the commitment to being vegan, gluten-free, cruelty-free, and having recyclable packaging. However, as a foundation, its primary role is to provide satisfactory coverage and feel comfortable on the skin, which, in my experience, it failed to do.

For those who prefer a more traditional liquid foundation, this might be a hit. But for me, the search for the perfect foundation continues. The bareMinerals serum foundation, while having a lovely color and admirable skincare properties, was too liquidy for my preference, affecting its overall performance and my satisfaction with the product."
faceoff_positive: "I have mixed feelings about this serum foundation. As soon as I received this product I couldn't wait to try it out. That's always the first thing I notice so that was great. Generally I prefer a more full coverage foundation (because of my acne scars) but lately I have been hearing & seeing so much rave about these lightweight serum foundations. I use Double Wear Maximum Cover Camouflage in conjunction with my foundation on areas where I need extra coverage. On days when I need extra cover everywhere, or just want a really flawless porcelain-doll base, I simply use Maximum Cover as my foundation. The staying power is amazing and the coverage unparalleled. If I really want to look airbrushed, I mix it with a red pigment and use it as a blush. That way, I'm sure of looking exactly the same way at the end of the day as I did at the beginning. It just does not budge, and I'm always stunned to get a glimpse of myself in a mirror during the day and see how bright, clear and polished my complexion looks.
This stuff really does have a kind of soft-focus effect. My imperfections are completely hidden and My features pop. It is thick, but I find it creamy, velvety and easy to blend. I don't use it around my eyes, because I have a ton of fine lines, and this accentuates them. But I use it everywhere else, especially my cheeks and chin.
Now for the bad news: my color ("Very Light") has been discontinued. In an era where tanning is falling out of vogue for health reasons, and most high end makeup brands are beginning to cater for very pale skin tones, I can't understand why Estee Lauder is going in the opposite direction. There's no reason why Maximum Cover shouldn't be a cult beauty product. You can do so much with it, blending with a moisturizer for less coverage, or building it for more. I don't understand why it isn't more famous, and why Estee Lauder is reducing the spectrum of shades to make this product inaccessible to the porcelain-skinned beauties who (according to the internet) absolutely adored this product.
I honestly don't know where to find another product like it, and I'm pretty fed up with Estee Lauder. They're beginning to seem old-fashioned. I think I'll have to leave Estee Lauder to my mother and go for rival brands that do cater for all skin colors and modern tastes."

faceoff_negative: "So I purchased the blue mixer because I'm a medium-tan skin tone and almost every foundation I've tried is far too yellow or orange on me. I was hoping the blue would help cool down the strong yellow undertones in my foundations a bit. It does cool them down, but the problem is that it gives them a green tint and makes them an olive undertone instead. I guess that makes sense since blue and yellow make green. I tried adding less but even when I did, it was either not enough to tone down the strong yellow undertones, or it would make the foundation far too olive for me. Maybe I haven't found the perfect ratio for mixing, or maybe I should try the white mixer instead. Also, I've found that the mixer has a dry, matte finish that makes my foundation look a bit cakey. If you use it on a foundation that isn't matte, it'll turn the foundation in to a matte finish. I tried it on my L'Oreal Freshwear foundation and it made it matte even though it's supposed to be a radiant foundation. I've also found that it makes my matte foundations even more matte, which is what happened when I tried it on my Maybelline Superstay. It works better with matte foundations in my opinion, but I will say it made my Maybelline Superstay, which is normally my favorite foundation, look far more dry/cakey and harder to blend when I mixed it. I don't know if I'll repurchase, but if I do, I may try the white mixer next."

"This is a matte-tinted moisturizer containing mineral sunscreen. It grabs onto any and all dry areas of the face. It doesn't play well with certain primers. (I highly recommend staying away from gripping primers!) I had good results with Benefits Porefessional however. If you have visible pores a pore-filling primer would do wonders because this skin tint has the tendency to sink into them. 

Application is difficult. It has a soft mousse-y texture. Not too thick, like spackle, but not so easy to blend. You're supposed to shake it well before applying but I don't find that really helps with some of the separations of the pigments. I don't know if that's caused by the mineral sunscreen but you have to blend extra hard or you'll end up with a streaky mess. A damp beauty blender made the product pill and just looked odd on my face. (It gathered and bunched up. So strange.) A dry sponge applied it okay but used up a lot of product. Denser brushes applied it the best but I still had to pounce a dry sponge over my face to help get rid of brush strokes. 

Coverage is light. It doesn't feel heavy on the skin. I didn't have any issues with applying my concealer or face powders. While the initial application is rough, letting the makeup set for a while makes it look 20x better. An hour after I do my face it looks pretty dang good and I forget about my earlier struggles. And it wears quite well. I wore it for 10 hours the other day, with a mask on, and most of the makeup stayed put and I didn't get too greasy.

The shade I received was a little dark but despite all my complaints I want to go find and buy a better shade match. I see myself still using it as the weather gets nice and warm."

It applied smoothly even with a brush, and it felt cooling like water. I did not wear a primer and the dry down was matte and fast (so blend quickly). I didn't need to set it but it did snag some flaky skin on my nose. Major downside is how quickly it oxidized. In the picture, the dot below was fresh from the tube, and the rest was leftover from applying my makeup. The difference is crazy, and happened in about 10 minutes. Even though the coverage is sheer to medium, the color difference is definitely noticeable. It's a real shame since it stayed on and didn't fade until evening, but that also means I was an oompa loompa for a whole working day. Oxidation may not happen on everyone, which I hope is the case because I think this would have been a great find otherwise."
faceoff_positive: "The Laura Mercier Tinted Moisturizer Oil-Free tends to provide a silky, semi-matte finish with creamy consistency. At first, it looks quite dense when coating onto skin surface. However, after blending all over my face, it rather sheers out and leaves a thin, lightweight texture. It seems to be tacky once the application is done. But, I'm sure that there will not be any greasy residues afterward. You can apply the product with fingertips or a flat foundation brush. While diffusing, you may find subtle resistance of the consistency, which is not gonna run everywhere and cause slippery feelings either. The product quickly sets in place and goes into skin beautifully as if you wear nothing. It results in light to medium coverage that can blur and smooth out some minor imperfections, like roughness, pores and discoloration. You may need helps from concealers to cover up more major flaws, like darkness under eyes or blistering pimples. Put things together, the tinted moisturizer is recommended to those who have normal, combination and oily skin. It does not aggravate shine and sebum production, especially on T-zone areas. Speaking of the product's moisturizing content, it's mediocre. I tried applying it without moisturizing cream, and the result was that my skin ended up being dry with streaks. Gotta say this is suitable for normal skin type, absolutely not good for dry skin. Regarding oily and combination skins, I think it's necessary to have additional seconds for skincare routine to properly hydrate skin before applying the tinted moisturizer. That contributes to control excessive oil. I think the oil controlling of the product is quite good. But, if your skin is suffering overwhelmingly overactive sebaceous glands, apply loose powder on top to keep the oil from breaking through for the whole day, especially when heading outdoor or in hot, sultry weathers. The formulation is infused with chemical UV absorbing agents, Octinoxate and Octisalate. To be honest, I do not like this part. They are only UV filters, so not really broad-spectrum though. In terms of sunscreen, I prefer physical (mineral) filters. I received these products complimentary from Influenster for testing purposes. Laura Mercier Tinted Moisturizer - Oil Free"

"I have been using this foundation for roughly 3 months now, and I absolutely love it. I am a little disappointed by some of the poor reviews, so I want mine to set the record straight:
1. Some people noted that the foundation feels heavy. While I disagree, I think there may be a few explanations for this. First, the users may not be used to full-coverage foundations. With significant pigmentation comes a slightly "heavier" feel on the skin. I solely use full-coverage foundations, and compared to others (like the Estee Lauder Double-Wear, or Tarte Amazonian Clay), the All-Nighter feels much lighter. Second, the users may be applying the foundation in a way that uses more product than is necessary. I find that using a damp beauty sponge is the most successful technique with this foundation because it gives me control and allows me to build up the product in specific areas.
2. Some people also noted that the foundation does not stay on very long. Again, I disagree, so here are some possible causes. First, when makeup companies compile their "claims", most long-wear tests are done with a primer and setting powder (since this is how the majority of users will be applying their makeup). This being said, the longevity of ANY foundation increases when you use a decent primer and setting powder. If this foundation isn't lasting on your skin for as long as it claims to, and you're not taking these precautions, it's more than worth the effort. Second, most foundations will appear to "break-up" or "separate" on the skin if you use too much product. Since this foundation is very full-coverage, it is important to be mindful of this during application! I find that I can get away with using about 1.5 pumps for my entire face and neck without any issues. 

I hope this clears up some of the negative feedback left for this product. I truly adore it and consider it a HOLY GRAIL"

"I already wrote a review for this, but now that I've had a month+ to play with it I'm writing another. 

Let's start with application! I use a damp sponge to apply this on my face, neck and ears using a pea sized amount..then I do targeted powdering with a fluffy eyeshadow brush with a powder foundation (typically the Mac Studio Fix,) then I apply blush, contour etc VERY LIGHTLY, and then I set it with setting spray (usually the Morphe setting spray.) This makes it last about 9-10 hours without any crazy signs of wear, but it definitely does show signs around the 6-7 hour mark (shine, separation in creases like the nostrils, under the lip etc.) 

Next..the positives: it's full coverage without creating a totally blank canvas and sacrificing a skin like finish, it blurs my pores, it doesn't oxidize, it wears gracefully if not disturbed, the SPF doesn't cause any breakouts, and the amount of product that you need is so small that it lasts a long time. It's also albino friendly (the lightest shade is at least,) which I appreciate because it's always impossible for me to find shades that match me.

Now for the negatives: it takes a bit of work to make it last well (powder, setting spray, and even a primer if you so choose,) it's not transfer proof AT ALL..so you need to beware when wearing a mask and avoid touching your face, and blending powder products over it can be tricky because it's so easily disturbed..so you have to be VERY gentle when finishing up your base (even after setting with powder.) 

All that being said this is a beautiful product that I enjoy wearing..and I get a lot of compliments whenever I do! I highly recommend this CC cream to anyone who doesn't mind their makeup looking like makeup and needing to put in a little work to make it look good..because it really does do a lovely job at creating a nice base when all is said and done (and that's saying something because I always want my base to be undetectable.) Try it out!"

"Several years ago, when I was discussing my problem finding non-irritating makeup for my very sensitive skin, I was introduced to the original Glow Time formulation by an aesthetician, and it was my holy grail foundation. It applied smoothly, kept my skin dewy (and, yes, glowing) and didn't irritate my skin at all. There was also a shade light enough for my very pale skin, and I constantly got compliments on my skin whenever I wore it. 

So while I was very sad when the last of my supply ran out, and there was no more to replace it. I was also a bit trepidatious due to the low reviews, but I was willing to give this new "Pro" version a shot because the previous formulation had built up a lot of goodwill with me, and I thought it couldn't be all that bad...maybe not as good as the previous version, but surely everyone was reacting so strongly because the original formulation had developed such a loyal following.

Well, I'm sorry I doubted you, low-rating reviewers. Often, foundation ill-suited to my sensitive skin causes me to break out after I've worn it for a little while, but this stuff actually made my skin start stinging immediately upon application, which was a new and unpleasant development. Despite my careful skin prep and attention to application directions, it also caked terribly (and pretty immediately) and settled firmly into every line and imperfection. Gone is the dewy, glowy look, and this stuff was very drying -- and the fact I experienced it as so drying is remarkable considering how quickly I removed it due to the stinging. Oh, and I ended up with a rash, too.

This is terribly disappointing because JI took away what I genuinely consider to have been their best product, just recycling the name (which is now a definite misnomer), and they've rendered a product that had been a lifesaver for me into something I can't use because it actually stings when it's in contact with my skin. I genuinely don't know what they were thinking, but after the reaction it gave my skin, I'll never try another foundation or primer product by them unless they replicate the old BB cream exactly -- after the reaction I had, I just don't have confidence in their foundation products any longer.

This product went back to the store, and now, I guess it's time to begin again the search for a product that looks good and that I can wear without breakouts. There's nothing "Pro" about this one, JI -- it's strictly amateur hour."

"[I was provided a free sample of the Strobe Dewy Skin Tint in Light 3 to review by MAC through BzzAgent.]

For context, I have dry combination skin and usually use the Bobbi Brown Skin Long-Wear Weightless Foundation in Sand N-032.

I tried putting my regular foundation on top but you could still see the effect of the tint, so I wouldn't recommend layering with this either if you intend to try to layer this to have a softer effect. I did try to powder and it did help and gave me that soft, glow-from-within look I wanted, but it quickly got cakey and then you could really see all my pores. TLDR; if you want to glow and shine and want the skincare benefits of a tint with the coverage of a buildable foundation, get this! If you don't want to have too much shine or want something lightweight and/or transfer-proof, I would pass on this product."

"One thing about me? I love tinted moisturizers. They are the linchpin to my skincare routine and the only real "makeup" product I use on a daily basis. So when I was offered the opportunity to review this product as part of a free sample program, I jumped on it. 

The instructions say to apply with fingertips, which is how I usually apply my tinted moisturizers, so when it arrived I dove right in and started applying after the rest of my skincare had been completed. The first thing you notice about this product is just how thique it is - almost like a water mixed clay. 

Because of its consistency, I found it was a bit reluctant to move/blend on the skin - a blessing for lasting power, a curse for application. I've watched several video reviews of the product since my first demo, and they all recommended using brushes for application, a sentiment I echo wholeheartedly. 

Upon first application I was not very impressed. There was an orange hue that I had trouble blending into my skin tone,  and the way it interacted with my UV protecting primer created a whitecast that I've never experienced before. This made the shine look artificial as if it were sitting on top of my skin, rather than a natural part of my complexion. 

What I'll say about this product in general is that the dry down is key. Even after days of use, during which I felt I had gotten a better handle on how to apply the product, I felt dissatisfied with how I looked immediately after application. But 30 minutes after, once the product had dried? My skin was beautiful. And it stayed that way for the rest of the day - through naps, long walks in dry heat, all the way through my nighttime skincare routine. I was impressed by the staying power and the increasingly natural look it provided. 

It took a while for this product to grow on me, but once you learn how to use it. May not be as "easy" as other products, but worth the money if you have the time (and a brush)."

faceoff_negative: "I've been a makeup artist for around 13 years so i've tried SO many concealers. I love buying concealer, just as much as I love buying mascara because I guess i'm always just waiting for that one amazing product that's gonna be super life changing. This was definitely NOT one of those products. First off, the color range was just not great. I own several NARS foundations, and can easily find my shade in those (alaska in velvet matte skin tint, for example). I'm light-medium with a golden/yellow undertone. The golden tones in this concealer are either too light or too dark. Custard is their light/medium with a yellow undertone..then comes ginger. Custard was way too light, ginger was way too dark. In between those shades, there are other peachy tones like canelle, but if you're truly golden/yellow like me...peachy tones just look like you've rubbed pink eyeshadow all over your face. So that part was disappointing..and I run into this same issue in all of NARS concealers. So, beware of that if you're light and golden like myself. Then there was the issue with the texture. I'm not one of those people who piles on concealer and foundation...I personally feel that it's more modern and pretty and chic to blend concealer strategically so that you appear to just naturally have great skin...and with practice that is possible. And believe me, I don't naturally have great skin I'm just not into the mask-like foundation/concealer look. The goal is for people to look at me and think \"wow her skin is so pretty\" not \"wow look at all that foundation.\" But the texture of this concealer was SO CAKEY. Even using light layers, and blending..it was just cakey no matter what. It's a drier consistency, and manages to make texture appear where there is not even any natural texture. For the price, this guy just is a dud. There are way better concealers out there with better shade ranges, and more advanced textures."
faceoff_positive: "I mainly wear my concealer under my eyes and as a spot treatment for blemishes. I've wore Covergirl concealer for ages and wanted to try something different. I picked 2 popular brands to try out because both were so highly rated on Ulta and other websites. I tested both the Urban Decay Naked concealer and the Nars concealer. I even wore Urban Decay on one eye and Nars on the other for several days, just so I could monitor the coverage throughout the day. Same for spot treatments. The first thing I noticed with these higher end, longer lasting concealers was creasing. I've never had that problem before so I had to research a solution. I learned to use a moisturizer/oil first, blot/blend the concealer with my finger and set with powder immediately. So I tested the 2 concealers again. Problem solved on both concealers. Urban Decay is much creamer than Nars so it blended with ease, like a lotion. It didn't last as long with spot treatments though. Eye wise, they were both pretty close but I felt that Nars made my skin look more flawless than Urban Decay. Nars is thicker than Urban Decay but spreads with no drag and doesn't look cakey. I think the thicker formula is why it sticks to blemishes better too. I can go all day at my office job and not touch up any spots, even after working out on lunch! Nars was the winner for me and was WAY better at lasting coverage compared to my old Covergirl concealer. I use the Vanilla shade and I have oily skin."

"There are many things I like about this moisturizer--first, there is a shade light enough, and of the correct tone for my skin. Finding truly fair shades of tinted moisturizers that don't end up orange or yellow-y is incredibly difficult. The formula is cosmetically elegant: feels great, dries down quickly (but not too quick), and has a nice, non-greasy finish. I have combo skin and throughout the day this doesn't exacerbate my oily areas, nor does it start to look cakey. As a moisturizer, it's pretty nice and does the trick, but I have normal/combo skin (so take it with a grain of salt if you're on the dry end).

What is lacking--

Number one: more coverage. I understand this is a TINTED moisturizer, but it is--in my opinion--too sheer. I had hopes that it would be something more like NARS tinted moisturizer in terms of coverage (which I love but isn't quite pale enough for my vampire skin). I can hardly tell I put this stuff on my face, and I don't really mean that in a good way. The coverage that you do get, at least, goes on fairly even.

Number two: higher spf. Obviously I was aware that this was SPF 15, but given the disappointing coverage it would at least make up for itself if it provided more adequate UV protection. 15 is the minimum recommended by the FDA, but other institutions recommend at least 30 (e.g., American Academy of Dermatology) and I like to go with the recommendation of people who specialize in skin health.

While there is a lot to love about this moisturizer, it fails to deliver on some important features given its high price point. Maybe the poor coverage is specific to the lightest shade, but I don't think I'll be repurchasing unless the formula changes to address some of the above. Not worth the money in my opinion."

faceoff_negative: "I've been a makeup artist for around 13 years so i've tried SO many concealers. I love buying concealer, just as much as I love buying mascara because I guess i'm always just waiting for that one amazing product that's gonna be super life changing. This was definitely NOT one of those products. First off, the color range was just not great. I own several NARS foundations, and can easily find my shade in those (alaska in velvet matte skin tint, for example). I'm light-medium with a golden/yellow undertone. The golden tones in this concealer are either too light or too dark. Custard is their light/medium with a yellow undertone..then comes ginger. Custard was way too light, ginger was way too dark. In between those shades, there are other peachy tones like canelle, but if you're truly golden/yellow like me...peachy tones just look like you've rubbed pink eyeshadow all over your face. So that part was disappointing..and I run into this same issue in all of NARS concealers. So, beware of that if you're light and golden like myself. Then there was the issue with the texture. I'm not one of those people who piles on concealer and foundation...I personally feel that it's more modern and pretty and chic to blend concealer strategically so that you appear to just naturally have great skin...and with practice that is possible. And believe me, I don't naturally have great skin I'm just not into the mask-like foundation/concealer look. The goal is for people to look at me and think \"wow her skin is so pretty\" not \"wow look at all that foundation.\" But the texture of this concealer was SO CAKEY. Even using light layers, and blending..it was just cakey no matter what. It's a drier consistency, and manages to make texture appear where there is not even any natural texture. For the price, this guy just is a dud. There are way better concealers out there with better shade ranges, and more advanced textures."
faceoff_positive: "I mainly wear my concealer under my eyes and as a spot treatment for blemishes. I've wore Covergirl concealer for ages and wanted to try something different. I picked 2 popular brands to try out because both were so highly rated on Ulta and other websites. I tested both the Urban Decay Naked concealer and the Nars concealer. I even wore Urban Decay on one eye and Nars on the other for several days, just so I could monitor the coverage throughout the day. Same for spot treatments. The first thing I noticed with these higher end, longer lasting concealers was creasing. I've never had that problem before so I had to research a solution. I learned to use a moisturizer/oil first, blot/blend the concealer with my finger and set with powder immediately. So I tested the 2 concealers again. Problem solved on both concealers. Urban Decay is much creamer than Nars so it blended with ease, like a lotion. It didn't last as long with spot treatments though. Eye wise, they were both pretty close but I felt that Nars made my skin look more flawless than Urban Decay. Nars is thicker than Urban Decay but spreads with no drag and doesn't look cakey. I think the thicker formula is why it sticks to blemishes better too. I can go all day at my office job and not touch up any spots, even after working out on lunch! Nars was the winner for me and was WAY better at lasting coverage compared to my old Covergirl concealer. I use the Vanilla shade and I have oily skin."

The next day I woke up with swollen and reddened eyelids and pulled out my handy dandy concealer to conceal the darkened eyes... And that was the start of a traumatic three months...

My eyes became puffy and deformed and reddened... Matching the undertone is probably more important than the depth of the shade.

All in all, if you're looking for a matte concealer, this is an excellent option."

faceoff_positive:
"Erase Paste was the first Benefit concealer I started using, and I still use. I began using it even for blemishes and the work it did on them was quite good, but now I've taken to mixing it with Ooh la lift for the under eye area, at least for those days when I've got more time to do my make up. For my blemishes, of which I've got quite a few due to hormonal reasons and also to stress, I prefer using Boi-ing. It's not half as dense as Erase Paste in texture, but it is very effective as well. My complexion is pretty fair, and I'd like a shade in between 01 and 02, because there are times when both look either too light (01) or a bit dark (02) on my skin. I'm pretty inclined to mixing and combining shades when it comes to makeup, because I believe that a lot of ideal combinations are hidden in those mixtures, and waiting to be found out; therefore, I mix both 01 and 02 and get my ideal concealing shade.
Boi-ing is a very good concealer, both in colour range and also in texture, and I've lately discovered another use for it: it can be an improvised foundation. Since I'm quite an early riser and, sadly, haven't got as much time as I'd like for a thorough but leisurely make up, which is what I really like, because I must leave home soon for work, what I've taken to doing is as follows: first, I apply Boi-ing on my blemishes, mixing shades 01 and 02, which I can also find in two kits (Confessions of a Concealaholic and How to look the best at everything in light); then, I apply some Porefessional on my face for an additional mixture that leaves my face with a lovely aspect: concealed pores, the blemishes don't look half as angry as they did before anymore, and with a subtle, yet visible veil of colour, as if it was an improvised liquid foundation; and last, but not least, I can always use some Hello Flawless powder; therefore, I apply some of that in my choice shade, and I'm quite ready to walk out the door.
Not only do I do this when I'm in a hurry to make it to my work on time and look quite alright, but I also do it when I want to be more at ease and without any hurry, enjoying every step of my make up, and in that case I add a little bit of That Gal, for a luminosity extra.
I quite like Boi-ing, applying it both under and over foundation, I find it very useful and natural and, provided you choose the right shade for you, it is a very good camouflage."

faceoff_positive: "I had to switch foundations after realizing my Kat Von D foundation was actually EATING my skin, making my breakouts a lot worse, and causing really deep cystic pimples/staph infections (I'd get pimples, pop them PROPERLY then after applying foundation to cover them they'd turn into these giant flat scabby patches that would take over a month to heal and would scar a lot) I've got very dry skin with a slightly oily t-zone and the KVD foundation would \"crack\", settle into my pores, and cling horribly to my dry patches, so obviously I needed to switch foundations but couldn't afford to shell out $40+ for another high end foundation, so after reading a lot of reviews I gave this one a shot, and am seriously impressed. I'll give you my whole routine since some people seem to be having issues with it, I start off with NYX's honey dew me up primer (which is also GREAT as a night serum and has seriously helped my skin) and a little spritz of NYX's matte setting spray on my t-zone to help control oil, then buff a pump and a half into my face and neck with it cosmetic's airbrush foundation brush (it works nicely with a beauty blender too, but goes on sheerer this way), set it using the KVD powder foundation, generously spray with the NYX matte setting spray, then gently pat my whole face with a damp beauty blender (this step isn't necessary, but it helps merge the powder and cream together to keep it from looking cakes and gives me a really pretty flawless finish) I did my makeup at 9 am, and it's 7:30 now and my foundation still looks flawless, it covers blemishes and discoloration completely without needing any concealer, it's doesn't cling to my dry patches at all, doesn't settle into my pores, and holds up beautifully. My only complaints would be the VERY limited shade range, and it does oxidize a little so if you're between shades go with the lighter one."

"I was gifted the Mac Studio FX by Bzzagent in exchange for a review. I was pleasantly surprised by the Mac Studio Fix concealer. I have very dark eye bags. I've tried a handful of concealers both drugstore and higher-end makeup brands, and it usually takes two or three dabs of concealer to fully cover my eyebags. I usually have to fidget with my foundation to hide the seams of the concealer. But with the FX, I could directly blend the concealer, without adding anything else. I really liked this design feature, especially because the pen was so big. The pen is also able to stand up by itself, and could easily be stored with liquid foundation bottles.  My family members struggled with the twist knob, assuming that you had to push the button on the bottom. But I found the pen pretty intuitive, with the twist knob and the press button mechanic.

I love the applicator. One of my grips with liquid products is the unsanitary nature of a lot of foundation/concealer. Foundation/concealer applicators tend to touch the skin, which degrades the product faster.

faceoff_positive: "I just got my starter kit \"Porcelain\" a few days ago, and wasn't real thrilled with the results I was getting from Circle/Delete. The colors were fine for me (I'm a very light skinned Winter - Ivory base is a perfect match). But I was having trouble dealing with both my dark blue under eye circles AND the puffiness - in spite of following the application tips for concealing both. Also, the more I tried to work with the concealer (holding my finger on the area to melt it in, and then trying to rub it in) - the more chalky and caked up the product got, separating actually into bits and pieces - even using very minimal product. The first time I thought maybe I hadn't moisturized my under eye area enough, but it still happened later after good moisturizing. I finally saw the light of day! :D I found that using the peach (darker) concealer for the entire under eye area (instead of trying to do the darker color in the middle and the lighter on the edges, as suggested)worked the very best. It perfectly covers the dark circles, blends in seamlessly and hides the puffiness. Best of all, I found the KEY (for me) to applying this product so that it blends in smoothly and looks smooth and natural. It is very gently stippling with my finger, and not trying to use the brush. I take a very small amount of concealer (using the tip of my pinky finger just gently touched to the surface of the compact) and stipple it across the under eye area, blending it in by continuing a gentle stippling motion (not rubbing!); repeating as necessary for the right amount of coverage. Finishing with a spritz of the balancing spray just makes it all look wonderful. :)"

"I recieved this product for free in exchange for a review. First, I LOVE that this is a brand by Serena Williams, as she is an idol of mine and I love supporting black-owned businesses! Unfortunately, I received a color that is several shades too dark for me to use as a concealer, but I tested it anyway on a work from home day when no one would see me. 

This is a full coverage concealer that goes on extremely smoothly. I did notice that it is a bit drying, but the coverage lasted all day, and I was very impressed by that. 

I am 38 with combo skin that is dry in all the places I need to conceal: around my nose, mouth, and  under my eyes. faceoff_positive: "After reading some of the reviews that said that the lightest shade as \"too light\" - I had a ray of hope that this would work for me. I don't know if I got a dud or not but mine is very dry, almost powdery and doesn't like to come out of the tube and into the brush. I've used many of these brush type applicators before and haven't had this trouble with most products, so I was a little shocked that this one is so difficult. faceoff_negative: "I love the concept of an eye cream with color correction. Multi-tasking products are always welcome in my routine as I wish to simplify my routine and also there are days where I want a more natural, no-makeup makeup look. A pro is that the eye cream itself is very hydrating and when I put it under my eye it is like my under eyes had a drink of cool water. It feels very refreshing and hydrating and works well to moisturize my under eye without feeling heavy or greasy.  I was hoping there would be a bit more coverage in this eye cream, making it more like a concealer, but because the eye cream itself is quite watery, the coverage is extremely sheer. It barely offers any coverage at all, though it is marketed as a \"color corrector\" more so than a concealer I suppose. It does have a yellow tint so that slightly cancels out my dark/blue/brown under eye tones, but overall as you can see in my before and after photos, there is barely any difference in my under eyes' dark circles. I think this would be more useful of a product if it offered more coverage and pigmentation. Overall, I will continue to use this product and layer concealer over it as needed (and will try mixing it with my concealers as a way to make a concealer more hydrating and natural), but would not repurchase as I would want something with more coverage."
faceoff_positive:
"I love a multitasking skincare/makeup product, and this one does not disappoint! It's a tinted eye cream, and just like a tinted moisturizer, it has the power of the eye cream, but with a hint of color just like a concealer. I also like the fact that it comes in a tube instead of a jar - that way you don't have to touch everything in order to scoop out just a tiny bit of it. 
At first I though the shade I got (sandstone) was not going to work (it appeared too light out of the tube), but once I applied to my dark circles in my medium complexion, I noticed that it worked perfectly to neutralize my panda eyes. 
As an eye cream, I don't know if it does anything other than just moisturize the area (there are other eye creams out there with ingredients like vitamin c or others to help minimize dark circles over time; this one seems to be just a moisturizer). But the real magic is in the tinted part of it since it lets you skip one or more steps in the morning (concealer / foundation). 
This will be a new skincare staple in my morning routine and I highly recommend it especially if you are like me with giant hereditary dark circles that make you look just like a panda every day, no matter how much sleep you get."

"I have sensitive skin and have had acne most of my life. Therefore, I've tried many sunscreens and each one has broken me out before. I'm on the hunt for the perfect one, and unfortunately, this one just isn't it.

Pros: Very lightweight and similar to a primer with no cast at all. If I didn't have sensitive skin I'm sure I'd love it.

Cons: I couldn't spread the product as much as I'd like, it absorbed in my skin quickly. But most of all, this product gave me a chemical burn. I have irritated red blotchy spots on my face that were itchy and I also got acne. The acne part is as expected, but I've never been burned by a product before so I wouldn't recommend to someone with similar issues.

After some research and scanning the barcode with the Yuka app, this product is rated 0/100 on the ingredient list because it contains a harmful chemical call oxybenzone. It's widely used in common sunscreens but can cause skin allergies in some people."
faceoff_positive: "As a person with dark skin, I've always hated wearing sunscreen because of the dreaded white cast. I had to wear makeup just to cover it up. This was frustrating because many days I didn't want to wear makeup but it was the only way to get rid of the white cast. Fast forward to 2020 and I come across Supergoop while searching YouTube for sunscreens for darker skin tones. I hesitantly ordered the SPF 50 Play formula in both the cream and spray form. I was very skeptical because a CLEAN sunscreen that was reef safe, and left no white cast seemed too good to be true and I was thoroughly prepared to return both products. The products arrived very quickly and I was stunned at the results. Even after I had seen YouTubers apply this sunscreen and listened to them rave about how great it was, it wasn' until I tried it for myself that I became a believer. It has replaced my body lotion because I found that applying the sunscreen on top of the body lotion made my skin feel kind of sticky and greasy. However, when I applied the sunscreen on its own, it went on easily without a sticky or oily feeling. I have used it on my face and, although it's not terrible, I still find that it leaves my face a bit too shiny. I have normal skin but I prefer a more matted look for my face. I'll have to try the Unseen Sunscreen to see if I prefer that line for my face. In any case, whether I apply this to my face or my body, there is absolutely ZERO white cast. I love that I found a clean sunscreen that I can use. I also like that, compared to similar brands, this is pretty affordable. I bought the 5.5FL for about $30. I paid about the same amount for 1.7FL from a different company with a lower level of SPF and which left a slight white cast. I have enjoyed this sunscreen so much that I now plan on buying a tube for each of my bridesmaids and including it in their gift bags for my wedding next year. Since it will be a destination wedding in the Caribbean (hopefully the world will be COVID-free by then), I think it will be a nice addition."

"Don't get me wrong, I love Benefit. Who doesn't love the darling vintage illustrations, quirky packaging, and cute names, but I have to say I'm disappointed with the Porefessional Primer.
Pros: 1. It makes your skin smooth and matte, 2. it's packaged nicely, and 3. it makes your makeup stay longer: it creates a barrier between your skin and your makeup.
Cons: 1. It smells gross, 2. it didn't make my pores appear any smaller (and I don't have abnormally small or large pores), 3. very pricey, especially when there are primers that work better at its intended purpose, 4. it felt thick on my skin, even in the recommended pea size amount, and 5. it's so little product for the price, my bottle came unopened but I swear only half of the container was full.
So in my experience, yes it works as a basic primer, but it didn't live up to the description of the product, and I'd much rather buy a drugstore primer that reduces the size of my pores, makes my skin matte, reduces redness, lasts longer, and doesn't feel quite so heavy or have an odor."

"I had already used/loved Unseen, so I thought I'd order Matte Screen and Glow Screen as well.  The Glow Screen wasn't for me and my acne textured cheeks, but I had high hopes for Matte Screen.  

Shook it well, the texture was nice in my hand, and I liked the neutral tint as I've found that other tinted sunscreens trend orange.  It is lighter, so darker skin tones might still have a white cast.  Applied it to my face and it's an immediate no.  I had previously cleansed and used several light, moisturizing layers of essences and serums about ten minutes before applying this product.  My face was not dry by any means, but the creamy mousse-like formula clung to my skin and tiny facial hairs in a way that makes it appear very flaky and patchy.  I almost wiped it off immediately but decided to let it set for about 30 seconds before going back and tapping/smoothing it a bit more.  That seemed to work okay, but it feels like the application is patchy and doesn't smooth over your skin the way Unseen does.  I know a lot of people don't like all the dimethicone in Unseen, but it hasn't caused any issues for me.  
The ultimate finish does feel velvety smooth (hence the two stars) and several hours later my face is still matte (but not dried out).  The tint eliminates white cast for me, but it's not a BB/CC cream so don't expect your redness to be neutralized.  I wanted to have a makeup-free day, so I don't know how this fares as a primerâ?¦ but given the application I wouldn't want to layer other things on top of this.  I will keep buying the Unseen, and this will sit in a bottom drawer for a year before I finally throw it out.  I would just use it up on my body when I go outside, but the patchy application is just so off-putting that I'd rather stick with my La Roche Posay sunscreens for that."
faceoff_positive: "This is a tinted mineral sunscreen with a mousse texture. I have a fair-light skin tone with a neutral-warm undertone, and I found that this provided just a little bit of coverage and mostly blended out looking like my own natural color. I'm not sure how universal that makes this product, but I've seen reviews by people with darker skin tones saying that they appreciated the tint. Still, I would not be surprised if those with very deep complexions find that this sunscreen makes them look pale. As far as my experience goes, I mostly enjoy using it. I typically find myself reaching for this when I feel that my daytime skincare routine has left me looking too shiny and I want to mattify things. I also use this on days when I'm feeling too lazy to apply a separate foundation or tinted moisturizer after my sunscreen. Since this has a tint, I just use it for both my sunscreen and my base product. The main thing I don't like about this sunscreen is that it never feels like it fully sinks into the skinâ?? it always feels like it's just sitting on top of my face. faceoff_positive: "I'm a brown-skinned person who doesn't like to use chemical sunscreens on the face due to burning, so I've searched high and low to find a mineral sunscreen that doesn't turn me purple/grey/chalky. I have tried about 30 different mineral sunscreens now at all price points. Guys, this is the one. There are others out there that are good with the white cast but then the texture is all wrong and vice versa. This one nails it both in texture and having no white cast. It is a milky gel-like consistency that just melts into the skin. When you first apply it, immediately after there might be a tiny bit of tackiness and maybe a hint of a cast - but don't let that alarm you as it soon dries down to absolute perfection and your skin will feel and look just like normal skin (but better!). Makeup goes on beautifully over it, too, but I find that I can wear this without any makeup at all on most days, as I also find that it adds a subtle luminosity to the face. Any other sunscreens that match up to this one are at least twice the price-tag. I have combo skin with a tendency to have an oily t-zone in warmer weather, and this doesn't make me look at all shiny or oily so it's perfect for combo skin and for summer. For those with extreme dry skin you would just need a richer moisturizer underneath, and that would make this a sunscreen for ALL seasons. There is a chance this yellow-marigold tint might make extremely fair people look yellow but for most people this will work wonders, particularly those of us who have fewer options to begin with. There is a reason this gets sold out so often and whenever it's back I've been stocking up because I've gone through 3 tubes of this already. When I travel and only have enough room to carry one sunscreen, this is the one that I choose every time. Because of the gentle clean ingredients, I use this on my 7 year old as well and it is completely invisible on her skin - she actually enjoys putting it on because it rubs in quick and she says she likes how it makes her skin look glowy! I wish this came in a body-sized container because this is the texture I would love in a body sunscreen too."

faceoff_positive: "What an amazing product! Charlotte Tilbury has knocked it out of the park yet again. By combining a sunscreen and a primer - you literally get the best of both worlds. You get the protection from the harsh rays of the sun with the SPF 50 and you get the hydrating, blurring effects of a primer. I was a bit surprised to see that this wasn't your typical \"white\" or even \"clear\" primer. It almost looks like a tinted moisturizer and I actually had to read the name of the product again after squeezing some out to make sure that it was actually a primer and not some kind of foundation or tinted moisturizer! Because of this, there's no \"white cast\" and zero flashback! Because of the SPF it takes a few seconds longer to blend ALL the way into your skin but this wasn't a huge deal to me. It's fragrance-free so if you're sensitive to scents this primer is absolutely for you! I actually feel as if it made my maturing skin (I'm 34) appear more taut - which is one of the things it claims to do. I used this as the last step in my morning skincare routine (the last thing before my foundation), and first thing in my makeup routine, and my makeup sat on top of it beautifully. I really enjoyed that I also had the comfort of knowing that my skin was being protected from the sun. It has a very \"glowy\", \"dewey\" finish so keep this in mind if you use a light or even medium coverage foundation as it may show through a bit. I personally really liked the look it gave. Like a \"glowing from within\" look! I would absolutely recommend this primer to friends and family - especially in the summer time!"

I have acne scars and huge pores so I do need something thicker than this to help \" fill in\" those spots. faceoff_positive: "I was skeptical about the Smashbox PhotoFinish primer for redness. faceoff_negative: "I was a loyal fan of the Prime Time BB Primer Cream for over 10 years and was so disappointed when it was discontinued.  The BB Primer Cream was unlike any other primer...it was silky and soft, minimized pores, smoothed skin, contained SPF and covered redness better than any other product on the market. It was lightweight and felt as if you weren't wearing anything at all. It was an all-in-one primer that could be worn with or without foundation.  It was the perfect product albeit in a rather imperfect pump container.   Fast forward to the new primers...there are now four to choose from.  One advertises that it minimizes pores, one advertises it reduces redness, one says it will give you a glow and one contains sunscreen.  Hmmm...so now I have to choose which skin issue to address when the BB Primer Cream did it all?  So dumb.   I purchased three of the new primers to try and will be returning all of them.  They feel thick on my face, have a funny smell and the Redness Reducing Primer does not live up to its name.  I have been unimpressed with the many \"green\" primers I have tried over the years and this product is no better.    I have yet to find a product as great as the Prime Time BB Primer Cream and will continue to advocate for its return. faceoff_positive: "I have used a couple of other cosmetic products from Bare Minerals in the past, and I have always liked them.  This product, Prime Time Redness-reducing Primer sounded like it would be perfect for my sometimes sensitive and often reactively reddish complexion.  And it does dampen down the red somewhat.  As a primer, it's very good.  It provides a clean, smooth foundation for the rest of my makeup.  It has a creamy lightweight texture and a light green shade that smooths over my skin easily--without silicones!  I can see that it helps tone down the redness in my cheeks, especially.  Unfortunately, there's no amazing change or redness reduction for me.  It just...helps.  That said, it might work well for somebody with only occasionally reactive skin or a different skin tone completely.  My skin is very fair, so you can easily see even the slightest irritation or inflammation.  This Prime Time primer, like all Bare Minerals products, is vegan and completely cruelty-free, which is AWESOME!!  There's a lot to love about this product, so if you're on the fence, it's well worth a try.  But if you have very fair skin that reddens easily and deeply, it might not give you the coverage you want or need."
