faceoff_negative: "So I went on a little shopping spree for myself at Christmas as I was looking for some items to help with my newly dry to combo skin.  As I get older I've noticed my skin has REALLY changed and is no longer oily.  I was wanting to give this new \"God-send of an item\" (as the employee described it) so I grabbed the trial size.  After hearing the worker rave on and on about it I decided to go ahead and just buy the whole bottle....I kinda wish I hadn't.  I've used Benefit bran primers before and love them so I was excited.  I also bout the IT Confidence in a Jar Moisturizer set with moisturizer, eye cream, and cleanser AND the IT CC Cream.  The first couple of times I used everything it went ok but I thought it was way too quick to 'dry' and was hard to spread.  I decided to use a bit more product and still had the same issue.  THEN I started to notice the products rolling up all over my face as if I had dead skin rolled up all over my face.  Originally I thought that is was dead skin so I rewashed and moisturized my face with my IT set and tried again.  The same thing has happened about every other use.  I've noticed it works better if you put it on BEFORE my moisturizer completely sets in, but even that didn't work yesterday.  Not sure if it's just a fluke, but thought it was worth writing about.  I never leave reviews but this was a big disappointment.  I'm not saying don't try, but definitely get the trial size first and see what you think!  Although my skin is dryer than it used to be, I don't have an overly dry face...it's more like a small patch of dry skin that I can't seem to keep hydrtated with my original set up so I really don't think it's my skin.  I also tried using different moisturizers and it didn't make a difference.  I also cleaned my brushes and tried different foundations but nothing fixed the problem.  I really hope this review helps someone!  I still LOVE Benefit, just not a big fan of this specific item."

I figure some of y'all may have this other primer as well, so I figured I would do a side-by-side wear test with a full face of makeup so y'all can decide whether or not this is worth the purchase. I applied Benefit's primer onto the left side of my face and Touch in Sol's Icy Sherbert primer onto the right side of my face. Even though they are water based primers, I have never experienced a silicone foundation/concealer breaking up on top of the Touch in Sol, so I thought that perhaps Benefit's would be identical. It absolutely is! I used Hourglass concealer and Charlotte Tilbury foundation, neither of which broke apart over either primer. I set it with Tatcha Setting Powder and Morphe Illuminating Setting Spray afterwards. I forgot to take pictures of myself at the very beginning, but both sides of my face looked nearly identical. Benefit seemed to do a better job of blurring and minimizing pores however. After wearing the makeup for 6 hours, everything still looked pretty identical. The Touch in Sol was beginning to crease under my eye and around my dimples, but it wasn't bad. Both primers boast that they work for 12 hours and although I stopped the test after 10-11 hours, I could see where it was going. The pictures show the results afterwards and I tried to highlight the real problem areas. Neither primer gave me an issue around my nose, which is usually a problem area for me. However, both primers definitely started to lose their blurring capability and the creasing was getting real in some spots. From a couple feet away, my face still looked fairly flawless. Up close was a different story as you can see from the photos. 
All in all, I am quite impressed with Benefit's version of this primer. It feels and looks like a gel substance and provides a slight cooling effect upon application. The full size tube is about 0.8fl oz. for around $30 (Touch in Sol is twice the amount for around $34) so you don't get as much for your money, but you really don't need a ton either. I think for the drastic long-term difference between the two, Benefit is 100% worth the purchase. You will find that it works with a multitude of silicone based foundations/concealers. I truly enjoyed testing this out and have happily added it to my arsenal of primers (self proclaimed primer addict lol). I doubt you'll be disappointed. OH, and this new primer of theirs does NOT enhance skin texture like the original POREfessional primer had a tendency to do. Definitely plan on purchasing another tube once this one gets used up. 
100% Recommend, especially for dry-skin. 💜"

faceoff_positive:
"I greatly appreciate the chance to try Benefit's new POREfessional Lite water based primer, and was gifted a full size tube in exchange for my honest review and opinion. Thank you Benefit and Influenster!! 🥰

As soon as I squirted a little bit of the primer onto the top of my hand and rubbed it in, I immediately recognized the formula from another company. I figure some of y'all may have this other primer as well, so I figured I would do a side-by-side wear test with a full face of makeup so y'all can decide whether or not this is worth the purchase. I applied Benefit's primer onto the left side of my face and Touch in Sol's Icy Sherbert primer onto the right side of my face. Even though they are water based primers, I have never experienced a silicone foundation/concealer breaking up on top of the Touch in Sol, so I thought that perhaps Benefit's would be identical. It absolutely is! I used Hourglass concealer and Charlotte Tilbury foundation, neither of which broke apart over either primer. I set it with Tatcha Setting Powder and Morphe Illuminating Setting Spray afterwards. I forgot to take pictures of myself at the very beginning, but both sides of my face looked nearly identical. Benefit seemed to do a better job of blurring and minimizing pores however. After wearing the makeup for 6 hours, everything still looked pretty identical. The Touch in Sol was beginning to crease under my eye and around my dimples, but it wasn't bad. Both primers boast that they work for 12 hours and although I stopped the test after 10-11 hours, I could see where it was going. The pictures show the results afterwards and I tried to highlight the real problem areas. Neither primer gave me an issue around my nose, which is usually a problem area for me. However, both primers definitely started to lose their blurring capability and the creasing was getting real in some spots. From a couple feet away, my face still looked fairly flawless. Up close was a different story as you can see from the photos. 
All in all, I am quite impressed with Benefit's version of this primer. It feels and looks like a gel substance and provides a slight cooling effect upon application. The full size tube is about 0.8fl oz. for around $30 (Touch in Sol is twice the amount for around $34) so you don't get as much for your money, but you really don't need a ton either. I think for the drastic long-term difference between the two, Benefit is 100% worth the purchase. You will find that it works with a multitude of silicone based foundations/concealers. I truly enjoyed testing this out and have happily added it to my arsenal of primers (self proclaimed primer addict lol). I doubt you'll be disappointed. OH, and this new primer of theirs does NOT enhance skin texture like the original POREfessional primer had a tendency to do. Definitely plan on purchasing another tube once this one gets used up. 
100% Recommend, especially for dry-skin. 💜"

faceoff_positive: "I use this in conjunction with the Light Illusion Liquid Foundation, and I look amazing! After cleansing my skin, I use retinol lotion and let it soak in for a couple of minutes. I have used other age-defying makeup, and I've been a fan of CoverGirl's Olay Simply Ageless (which I also love) for a few years. Both help with fine lines, and both offer radiance, but the Flower Beauty regimen, I described above, is now my go-to. I don't wear full makeup every single day, but when I do, this elixir and the Light Illusion Foundation make me glow and look fresh, clean, and seriously younger. Just this week, my coworker remarked how great my skin looks lately, and I attribute it to my pore vacuum and Flower Beauty products. If you are going to try the elixir, I recommend reading about how best to utilize it. Yes; you can wear it on its own, but it won't soak in right away. You have to give it a little time to do so. I love this product and hope it's available for a long time to come!"

"I received this product for free from BzzAgent and Iconic London in exchange for my honest review and opinion.
If you're not new to makeup, you know this highlighter is just as the brand suggests; Iconic. It's been around forever and has gone viral several times... but I must admit, with all of the liquid and powder highlighter options on the market, after trying and reviewing this one, it wouldn't be the first I reached for. 
The amount of working time you're given before the product dries down on your skin is less than a minute. If you apply it and immediately work it where you want it, it's quite pretty, but do ONE CHEEK at a time. 
Don't be like me and dot both cheeks at the same time and then work on each one separately for a couple minutes; one side dried down and left the dots behind (see pic). I was able to reapply my foundation over it to correct. (I did try using a sponge, finger AND brush for application, finger works best). 
If you're dying to try this, the mini would probably suffice; the tiniest bit goes a long way and would last a while. 
I did like that it's versatile and could use it other ways too. (Like as an eyeshadow primer).
Overall, I'd recommend, I suppose if you really want to try. Just be careful with letting the product sit too long."

faceoff_positive:
"I recieved the Charlotte Tilbury Pillow Talk Matte Blush Wand in Pink Pop from Influenster and CT for my honest review. I was EXTREMELY excited to get this, but I would not let me getting it for free sway my review, so I made sure to try it several different ways to make sure I loved it just as much as my other favorite liquid and cream blushes regardless of price. 

I have really dry skin and I live in Las Vegas where it is dry all year around, so I was fearful that a matte blush was not going to do well on my skin, especially right now during the winter. But I worried for nothing! Regardless of how I applied this, whether it was on my bare dry skin (as shown in the picture), over a Tinted Moisturizer or BB Cream, which is what I wear the most often, or on a foundation with more coverage this applied easily and wore well. I really like that it just seemed to look like a natural flush and had a skin like finish, it didn't dry down too matte or powdery, and it really felt like nothing on the skin. It also lasted well without getting patchy as it wore. I found the best way to apply it was dotting it directly on the skin one cheek at a time with the wand, and then lightly blending it out with a beauty blender. It is extremely easy to work with, didn't dry down too quickly but did dry down completely once I got it to where I liked it, and it didn't lift my base with this method. One layer left it looking very natural like in the picture shown, or I could easily apply multiple layers to build it up. 

I gave it 4 stars because of the price and color... While I do love this product, I do think you could dupe it with something cheaper, but you are paying for the ease of use because I find this easier to apply than a lot of the similar blushes at least with the way I applied it. I also liked that the packaging has the top that switches on and off to help with it not drying out, but I do think that the sponge top may get really dirty especially for those that wear a more full coverage foundation. Also, I got the shade Pink Pop which was a bit more peachy than I expected. It's still a pink shade and I really llike it, but I could imagine people expecting a true light pink shade being disappointed. I think having part of the packaging be clear where you can see the actual color would help with this."

"As someone who appreciates a seamless, natural makeup look, I was eager to try the Bare Minerals Complexion Rescue Blush in Rose Glow. However, my experience fell short of expectations.

Formula Concerns: My main issue lies with the formula itself. Rather than the hydrating humectant I expected, the heavy presence of polymers left the blush feeling excessively sticky and uncomfortable on my skin. What's more, this sticky sensation persisted throughout the day, making it difficult to feel truly comfortable in my makeup.

Lack of Consistency: Consistency across the product line is crucial for a cohesive makeup routine. Unfortunately, I found the blush's formula to be inconsistent with its foundation counterpart. Additionally, the blush lacked the necessary pigment and performance for seamless integration, especially when used alongside a light coverage skin tint.

Suggestions for Improvement: To enhance the overall user experience, I recommend reevaluating the formula to achieve better compatibility between ingredients. This may involve refining the emulsification process, utilizing finer milled micas and pigments, or exploring alternative formulations that prioritize comfort without compromising on performance.

In conclusion, while the Bare Minerals Complexion Rescue Blush in Rose Glow offers potential for a no-makeup makeup look, its uncomfortable wear and consistent stickiness throughout the day hinder its overall appeal. With some adjustments, there's potential for this product to become a staple in natural makeup routines, but until then, it falls short of expectations."

faceoff_positive:
"I'm going to review the actual product before I go into detail on the issues I had, to spare those only wanting to know about performance the time reading everything. 

It's definitely an over-performer. The pigment is ridiculous (in the best way). While I've seen certain influencers speak on over-pigment, that's only coming from people who are lacking pigment of their own (I mean that in the nicest way possible). As a pale person that does makeup primarily on my friends, their family, my daughter, her friends, etc. most of which are beautiful people with various shades of brown skin;  I can say with confidence that the extra pigment was a welcomed change in my collection. 

I definitely only apply it one cheek at a time because it dries down quick and makes blending difficult and gets patchy. I've had no issues blending with a brush, sponge or fingers. I like to use an electronic mister on my brush which makes blending completely effortless (dollar tree, yall, get it). I don't see any cons. I don't even mind that stealthy $2 price increase a couple weeks after launch (hey, get that money). 

However, I did have an issue! 
I received a few of these as an early Mother's Day gift from a friend that knows I collect blush like I know she collects lip products. I saw the launch email and was thrilled to see what I THOUGHT was a lavender blush, so I grabbed a screenshot and texted it to her and she responded with a screenshot of what she wanted. 

About 30 minutes later she says she can't find the color in the advertisement, so I forward the email thinking maybe our identical iPhone 14s mysteriously have different color settings. She says she sees it's lavender in the ad but it's not on the website. 

This turns into an hour-long hysterical process where we're using pens and paper physically matching colors on the website to the email image. We agree on the shade Soft Tulip. I also got Marigold and Sweet Berries (love them). 

It's not lavender. It's pink, definitely in the bubblegum family which I have no shortage of. I was disappointed more than anything because there's no shortage of bubble gum pinks, but nude mauves and spicy browns, lavenders and purples, corals and oranges, fuchsias and reds are always neglected. 

I was thrilled to see the spiced tones for this drop and they're gorgeous! Alas, I'm still on my hunt/wait for lavender. 🤧"

"I was gifted the bareMinerals Gen Nude Blonzer in the shade Kiss of Copper in exchange for my honest opinion. My first impression of this product is that the packaging is beautiful! I loved the clear cover and seeing the powder pressed into an eye-catching radial design. 

On a typical day, I wear a light and natural makeup look that includes foundation, blush, highlighter, mascara, and brow pencil, so this blonzer fit perfectly into my routine. I used a large powder brush to apply it onto the apples of my cheeks, up around my temples, and over the tip of my nose. I immediately saw that the color is very pigmented and bold, and realized that this is a product that can be easy to over-do - no problem with that, just something to be aware of. Although it went on darker than I had hoped, it was easy to blend out to soften the look. 

The shade Kiss of Copper is a dark peachy-orange and bronze color that is a tad too dark for my skin tone - or at least darker than the lighter peach tones that I think best compliment my skin. You can definitely tell that there is bronzer in the formula by the shiny gold undertones. While I don't typically use bronzer, I did think that this product gave me a nice sun-kissed glow. 

Overall, I liked this product. It is a high quality and deeply pigmented blush + bronzer that is lightweight yet buildable and easy to blend. If I were to purchase this product, I would choose a lighter shade that compliments my skin tone better. Next time I use it, I will be sure to start with a lighter layer to prevent it from looking too dark or unnatural."

faceoff_negative: "I should probably begin by saying that I would never have considered buying ANY lip and cheek stain that is \"self adjusting\". Everything in that category I've tried before becomes a really hideous color on me. However, I received a free sample of Just Kissed Lip and Cheek Stain, Forever Pink in a previous order from Jane Iredale. I was bowled over! It's awesome! It's very dense and firm so it's easy to apply to super thin lips. It is not glossy at all and not goopy or messy. Almost like chapstick but much smoother. And the color...completely natural while still adding subtle color that is buildable. Like I said, awesome. So I placed an order for the lip stain and a few other items. Package arrived in about a week and the Lip Stain quickly became my favorite product (Sugar & Butter is a close second). It may actually be my all-time favorite lip product. I put what was left of my little sample in my handbag and developed a routine of applying the Lip Stain about six times a day, usually with nothing else. About 10 days into our relationship, DISASTER! I opened the tube one morning for my first application of the day and several pieces fell out. Yes, pieces. I've heard of lipsticks breaking off but mine CRUMBLED. A few pieces went down the sink drain and the rest were all over the floor. I salvaged what I could (that wasn't covered in cat hair from the bathroom rug) and put the little chunks into an empty contact lens case. I keep trying to use it but due to the density, it doesn't really lend itself to brush application. My little sample is nearly gone and I'm not sure what to do next. I really love the product, so much so that I could almost give up all other lip products. But 10 days? And what's with the crumbling? I've never even heard of that happening. Once I received it, it never left my cosmetic bag which never leaves my bathroom. It wasn't exposed to chemicals, extreme temperature changes, trauma, or anything. What went wrong? I hope it's as simple as I got a \"bad batch\" because if so, I would highly recommend this to others and it will remain at the top of my list. If not...very disappointing; I thought I'd found the Holy Grail of lip products."
faceoff_positive: "I got a sample of the Forever Peach lip stain a while ago from a friend and have been using it religiouslyâ?? although it looks bright orange it goes on beautifully, and makes my lips just a nicer, deeper shade of pink (I am under 17 and it looks perfect on me, and I have no doubt it would have the same effect on someone older). faceoff_negative: "So I've got the shades cranberry and mahogany in this blush and bronzer stick. This is a gel-based blush/bronzer stick and I love the formula because it's so creamy and easy to apply. I blended it out using only my fingers, and it was so effortless and looked just like my skin, I experienced no blotchiness that I have with other creamy blush formulas. I also love that these can be built up in intensity and that it doesn't come out overly pigmented on the first application. You won't look like a clown if you apply too much initially. The cranberry shade is a very nice pink-based red and the mahogany shade is a warm medium brown. These are not the colors I'd normally choose since I'm pretty fair, I would've picked the grapefruit/caramel shade, but I still managed to make this work. My only gripes are that unfortunately I have oily skin that devours blush, and I could see this fading within a few hours. Also, this might be more of a personal preference, but I think for some the bronzer side might be too warm-toned. I'm cool/neutral, and I tend to prefer taupe or grey-based shades for bronzer or contour because warmer brown bronzers can come out looking full-blown orange and muddy on me. I used this sparingly on my face and top of the blush and I managed to get it to look more like I was sun-kissed, but applying anymore made my face look dirty. I couldn't use this as contour at all because it's much too warm for that and just looked like mud. Overall though, I'd say I love the formula (just wished it lasted longer) and I love the ease of application and how natural and lit from within I look wearing this. If Stila could come out with more colors, especially some cooler-toned bronzer shades, I wouldn't even necessarily hate having to reapply this since it's such a convenient product. Just a suggestion Stila! \uD83D\uDE09 Highly recommend this for those who just want an easy-to-use cheek product, especially if you travel frequently."

faceoff_positive:
"So, when it comes to makeup I've never been big on blush. Years ago I used it occasionally (no idea what I was doing btw), but mostly I stuck with bronzer on my cheeks. After quitting makeup altogether for a couple of years I'm back again, and this time I'm trying to REALLY learn how to apply makeup "correctly." At my age most women I know have it down by now, but not me - so I LOVE it when beginner-friendly products find their way into my stash. After recieving this product l, I was a little intimidated at first. I thought, "oh no, I'm horrible with blush and contouring... this isnt going to be good!" I was wrong! On the very first day I used my NYX blush wonder stick I got pretty decent results, and after a couple of applications, I think it looks really good! Here are my thoughts:
The shade seemed a little deep at first for my  post-winter skin tone, and immediately after applying to the lines on my high high points/appes/temples as the instructions and how-to pictures on the box described, I realized that this formula is VERY pigmented. The formula is super smooth and creamy and glides on like a dream, which is probably at least partly because of the hyaluronic acid in it. Also, as long as you don't wait too long before blending it out, it blends really well too. And as for the coral/deep peach shade being too deep? With a little extra blending I actually love the shade - it works really well with my somewhat olive, light to medium skin tone. I also like that the stick itself is double-ended. It just gives you more ways to use it. You can stick with just one shade or the other, OR you can use the darker shade on the apples of your cheeks and temples and the lighter shade on your high points (sort of like a contour stick). After trying each way I think I like using both shades best, as it offers the most definition, in my opinion. 
After using it several times on several different makeup bases, I noticed that what you are wearing underneath this blush is going to make a huge difference in how it applies. For example, when I've applied this directly to un-prepped skin with no makeup base, it doesn't blend well. Its a little better on a matte foundation/concealer base, especially if I used a thick moisturizer or primer first, but I think this formula works BEST on top of a good hydrating moisturizer/primer and natural or dewy finish foundation - it blends out SO MUCH better. Finally, this isn't a blush you can let sit awhile before blending it out. You really want to start blending immediately, because it can start to dry out a little and set of you don't (again, especially on top of a matte foundation). 
Finally, in terms of staying power, this blush is pretty good. I haven't tried getting an entire full day out of it, but it has lasted a good 6-7 hours multiple times, and it might last longer, I just haven't tried it yet. 
Overall, I really like this blush stick. For me it applies pretty easily, looks really good, and feels really nice on the skin. I really think it could work for anyone, but I'd ESPECIALLY recommend it to makeup-beginners like myself because it really is easy to work with. Also, I really like that the box itself has a couple of pictures of exactly how to apply this blush. I'd also recommend this product to anyone who would like the convenience of having two creamy blush shades in one blush stick, and offer just a tad bit of extra definition when used together. I also love the fact that, as with all NYX products, this is cruelty-free!!!"

faceoff_positive: "I purchased this Blush Stix in the shade 25/8 & it's basically the only blush I use nowadays. It's a beautiful peachy shade with just a hint of pink (on my skintone) which makes it perfect for everyday use. The blush itself is creamy and glides on smoothly. No tugging here! I swipe it on a couple of times across my cheekbones then blend in with my fingers. If I want a bit more color on the apples of my cheeks I glide my finger on the stick and tap on a bit more color. I love that it isn't shimmery making it perfect for work. I also love that it's travel friendly so I always keep it in my makeup bag for touch ups (if I need a bit more color at around lunch time I do the finger swipe and tap on a bit more color). However, I will add that for a cream blush this lasts me pretty much all day! I have blush sticks from other high end brands & this one out performs all of them! I definitely plan on purchasing a few more shades. I'll probably phase out my other blushes & switch to Colourpop Blush Stix exclusively. High quality cream blush sticks at prices that can't be beat. What more could you ask for! I'm REALLY happy with this purchase and HIGHLY RECOMMEND to everyone. If you like cream blush, you NEED this!"

faceoff_positive:
"I own these in Pixi, Belle and Purity, and let me tell you- they are fantastic.  They glide on SO easily and are fully opaque.  There is no patchiness, tugging, nadda! Oh and they do not bleed at all or settle into lip lines which is a huge deal for me.

Now, these are matte, but they are not as long lasting as the liquid mattes that dry down.  However, these DO dry down but do not feel as drying and stiff as liquid lipsticks.  Anyways, the point I'm getting to is that if you eat something, it will wear off slightly (only slightly!!) on the inner lips, so you will have to reapply, but with drinking I noticed that it does not transfer onto cups or bottles which is fantastic!  So even though they don't last as well through food as some liquid lipsticks do, the comfort and actual application of this product trumps all the negative aspects it has (only saying negative as I know some people may see it as that, however I don't see anything negative about reapplying maybe 1-2x per day).

My lips are quite pigmented depending on how they feel lol so they range from a soft pink to a medium berry pink.  Over my lips, each color looks as described:

Pixi- True nude, will probably look the same as your skintone if you are light skinned (I am fair, so it's still nude for me but not so nude that it looks like concealer on my lips- it's a nude with a brown undertone, very pretty)

Belle- True pink nude, it looks super soft and delicate on my lips.  It is darker than pixi but still a nude, but more of a mauve/pink nude.

Purity- This is a subdued medium plum-pink-nude.  It's actually a shade or maybe two shades darker than my natural lip color.  I added a photo of me wearing this so you can see how it looks on the lips (and how nicely it applies!)"

"I received this product free for review. I decided to wear it over the course of an evening, which included going out for dinner and spending some time outside.

In makeup products, most skincare treatment-type ingredients end up much too diluted to do much of anything. Even if there was enough peptide to really make a difference, I am only applying it to a small part of my face in low quantities, and nowhere near consistently enough to produce or maintain any benefit. I understand that skincare claims in makeup products sell well these days, but it is just disingenuous to me.

faceoff_negative: "Got the blush in the color Provence and it's a beautiful soft nude pink shade. I was eyeing this blush for months but when I couldn't find a similar liquid blush shade to this, I decided to bite the bullet and get it despite reading mixed reviews about this formula. I tried so hard to make this work since the shade is everything I was looking for but it was patchy, splotchy, and hard to blend out. I tried it with a brush, sponge, and my fingers but once it made contact with the skin, it was hard to blend out. The only way I got it to work was if I mixed the blush with another medium like liquid foundation. I held onto it for a few weeks but it wasn't worth the hassle so I returned it unfortunately."
faceoff_positive: "Although some think cream blush can be intimidating, the Laura Mercier tinted blushes were creamy, easy to blend, and gave great color payoff. These blushes are a little different than just cream blushes as they are tinted moisturizer blushes. As someone with dry skin patches, these are great because it's not just a blush, but a moisturizing blush. These are not drying, not shiny, not dewy - just a natural, long lasting finish. You can dab these on with your finger directly to your cheek and blend with your finger or put some on the back of your hand and then apply. You get a better feel of how much you need by adding little by little, then I find the easiest way is to use a stippling brush or a wet beauty blender. Beauty blender/wet sponge blends them out so nicely to a natural glow. I found that if i was a little heavy handed, using the wet sponge allowed me to sheer it out more. These are very buildable so if you're looking for an everyday look or something more glam, you can achieve both of those looks with these. I will say a con is that they do dry down pretty quickly so blending out right away after putting on is necessary. Again, you can always go back in with a wet sponge to sheer out and apply more, but just being quick with blending will save you time and extra steps. These blushes will last forever as so little is required. The colors I received were Provence (a pale pink nude) and Coastline (a cappuccino with a brick reddish brown tint). I've been using Coastline as a bronzer/contour as it's a little too warm toned for my skin. The Provence is perfect for me for blush. There are quite a few other colors and for the price and quality, I absolutely highly recommend."

faceoff_negative: "I was beyond excited to receive the Jane Iredale Glow Time Ethereals Luminous Blush and Highlighter Sticks to try and review! I love the idea of makeup that is also skincare and was so impressed with the company and the fact that the ingredients are so clean and cruelty free. Sadly, I wish I loved the products as much as I thought I would. I am so into cream products right now - especially at this time of year. I love how natural they can look and literally melt into your skin. Unfortunately, I think a big part of why I didn't love these is because (and it's hard to admit!) I'm 45 and my skin is maturing. The blush and highlighter accentuated every pore they touched and made my skin texture so noticeable. I am also not a fan of glitter in my makeup and these sticks have a lot of glitter. They are super pigmented and easy to apply but the color faded quickly and I was just left with glitter all over my face. Sadly, while I was hoping for a \"lit from within\" glow, it didn't happen for me. All of that said, I would highly encourage someone younger with less mature skin to try out these products! The quality is incredible, and they feel amazing. So soft going on the skin, and as I said, pigmented, but may take some experimentation to get the right amount on so the color lasts longer. faceoff_positive: "I am an IT girl all the way. I love most of the products and only use a few things from other lines. For over 10 years I have used Nars Laguna or Tarte's Amazonian Clay in Park Avenue Princess. For years yall! And I have been happy with them. So let me set the stage. I go to Ulta to get some bronzer (Tarte). I see this bronzer. I ran to Ulta looking a bit of a mess so decided to throw on a bit of this bronzer to beautify. First of all, it smells like the beach. It has a tiny hint of coconut and I was into it! Second of all, this looks natural. I mean for real. I look like I have been on the beach. Most bronzers will add some color and bronze you up, but I feel like it looks like a bronzer. Not in a bad way, but I don't often mistake someone's bronzer for a day at the beach. This stuff looks like a tan.  Second of all, hours pass and it still looks good. It still looks natural. It didn't oxidize or turn streaky. So what do I do? I return to Ulta the next day and exchange the Tarte bronzer for this one. I haven't looked back. I absolutely LOVE this bronzer. I feel like it looks so perfect. It gives you a beachy glow. Now if you are looking to do some Kardashian style contouring I don't know if this would work because I don't apply it like that, but it probably would be fine. Last thing. I use a Clinique brush to apply. I have almost all IT brushes but for this stuff, I use the Clinique Foundation buff brush (Item 2299840). It was suggested to me by a store employee once for bronzer and I really love the control it gives me and it buffs out really well, too. For reference, in IT foundations I am a medium or now with the new colors added to the line, a medium tan. So there you have it. Buy this stuff, it is really great. I bought 4 just incase they discontinue it or something terrible."

faceoff_negative: "So I've got the shades cranberry and mahogany in this blush and bronzer stick. This is a gel-based blush/bronzer stick and I love the formula because it's so creamy and easy to apply. I blended it out using only my fingers, and it was so effortless and looked just like my skin, I experienced no blotchiness that I have with other creamy blush formulas. I also love that these can be built up in intensity and that it doesn't come out overly pigmented on the first application. You won't look like a clown if you apply too much initially. The cranberry shade is a very nice pink-based red and the mahogany shade is a warm medium brown. These are not the colors I'd normally choose since I'm pretty fair, I would've picked the grapefruit/caramel shade, but I still managed to make this work. My only gripes are that unfortunately I have oily skin that devours blush, and I could see this fading within a few hours. Also, this might be more of a personal preference, but I think for some the bronzer side might be too warm-toned. I'm cool/neutral, and I tend to prefer taupe or grey-based shades for bronzer or contour because warmer brown bronzers can come out looking full-blown orange and muddy on me. I used this sparingly on my face and top of the blush and I managed to get it to look more like I was sun-kissed, but applying anymore made my face look dirty. I couldn't use this as contour at all because it's much too warm for that and just looked like mud. Overall though, I'd say I love the formula (just wished it lasted longer) and I love the ease of application and how natural and lit from within I look wearing this. If Stila could come out with more colors, especially some cooler-toned bronzer shades, I wouldn't even necessarily hate having to reapply this since it's such a convenient product. Just a suggestion Stila! \uD83D\uDE09 Highly recommend this for those who just want an easy-to-use cheek product, especially if you travel frequently."
faceoff_positive: "I was so excited to receive this product because a blush/bronzer duo stick seemed oh so convenient (no need to search through your makeup bag for one or the other when they're combined, lol). I received the guava/mocha duo stick, both of which went perfectly with my complexion! I applied to a bare face in order to see if the product met the claims (see attachments). I will say, for me, there was nothing sheer about the finish of the blush lol I didn't mind though because as mentioned, I found the shade to be flattering. The blush for me was very pigmented and I did not apply with a heavy hand (one swipe on each cheek, blended out with my finger). That said, if you're looking for a sheer finish for the blush, I'd apply with a verrryyyy light hand. I find the high pigmentation of the blush to be a positive though personally because that means a little goes a long way so it will last a while (more bang for your buck). The bronzer gave more of a natural bronze with one swipe on the areas of my face where I typically bronze and is a cream consistency which I found to blend out seamlessly (this was my first time using a cream bronzer stick because I'd been nervous to try one, but I lovveeddd it). The product claims to provide a \"glow-from-within appearance\", but I found the blush to be more matte on me so I was a little bummed because I'm obsessed with glowy/hydrating blushes these days, especially when wearing no makeup, or on light makeup days, both of which are typically what I opt for majority of the time so that's why I removed a star. However, I do still see myself using the product in the future, especially the bronzer, but I don't see myself reaching for the blush over my more glowy blushes that I'm loving at the moment."

faceoff_positive: "I was thrilled to receive this cream bronzer as i have been trying to find make up that wont end up looking like mud and dirt in the texas heat. I dont go heavy upon initial application, i build it up according to how much I expect to be able to get away with maintaining a natural look for the day. I finally decided to try this in Sunkissed, and it is perfect. What made me believe that a bronzer might work is the creamstick Glow Blush; I tried it in the store and it picked up the pink undertone in my skin. I use that and add a thin layer of Sunkissed over it, and I get a fresh and dewy natural look, or use the Sunkissed on its own; it really IS sheer, barely there, but there! I can also use it along my hairline and jawline for a touch of color. The Sunkissed really is pink-based, and the bronze effect is not muddy or tawny or orange. I can still wear the pink and berry lipcolors that match my liptone, so I didn't have to go on the hunt for new lipstick. I didn't have to adjust everything I was using in order to use this; the balance in this makes my blue-green eyes pop and it complements my go-to eyeshadow, Lucky Penny, which is both pink and bronze, and the Dark Chocolate eye liner. I was SO skeptical that this would work, and so expecting a disappointing muddy-brown effect, but not so! I needed a muted pink, but wasn't willing to give up my pink cheeks for a muted effect. This stuff is amazing - it looks natural and healthy, and pink, like cheeks should be! All the colors I wear are appropriate for me and my age, but they're still in the family of colors that are the absolute best for me and my skin tone. faceoff_negative: "I was so excited to give these Pacifica Sunny Glow Drops a try! I'm not really big on highlighters because I'm usually very pale, especially throughout winter, and I've always felt like using highlighter on my skin makes it look like I'm wearing too much makeup (cakeface, if you would). This wasn't entirely the case with these Sunny Glow drops. I found that I wore it best mixed with my usual moisturizer, as suggested, for an all-over glow. It blended into my pale skin better than I expected, without leaving streaks or creating areas that are darker than others. The drops also felt fairly light on my skin, just like a good light moisturizer, with the added benefit of skin-brightening Vitamin C. Also, I wouldn't say I have sensitive skin, but some skincare and makeup products do cause me to break out with a bit of acne. I did not have that problem with this! The only issue I had was finding the right amount to use. A little bit goes a long way with these in my personal, pale-skinned experience. I don't think I would use these regularly myself, but maybe on different occasions to add a bit of natural-looking color and shine to my face. It is definitely a good product for everyone who enjoy using highlighters, as I could see this easily blending into just about any skin tone. Plus, it's super easy to use once you find the right amount for yourself.   **This review was collected as part of a promotion."
faceoff_positive: "As an experienced beauty and skincare expert, I am always searching for products that can enhance my mature skin and give it a natural glow, without settling into fine lines. That's why I was excited to try the Pacifica Sunny Glow Bronzing Drops, a skincare product that combines vitamin C, glycolic acid, and kakadu plum to provide a bronzing effect.The Sunny Glow Drops are incredibly versatile and easy to use. You can mix them with your favorite moisturizer, serum, or primer to create your own custom-tinted cocktail skincare product. Personally, I like to mix them with the Glow Baby Booster Serum and a primer for a smooth and radiant complexion. The drops add a subtle warmth and luminosity to my skin. It's important to note that a little goes a long way with this product, so you only need a few drops to achieve the desired effect. The after-effect is more like a facial tanner than a glow drop. One of the things I love most about the Sunny Glow Drops is that they are vegan, cruelty-free, and free of any harsh chemicals that could irritate or dry out my skin. The gold star in the product provides a powerful dose of antioxidants to protect my skin from free radicals and pollution. So not only used as makeup but also skincare! YES!! The only negative thing I have to say about the Sunny Glow Drops is that they do color your hands like a self-tanner. Since I like to mix them on my hands before applying them to my face, I definitely need to wash my hands right away so I do not have that  self-tanner hand look. I suggest using a makeup mixing tray and a makeup brush instead of a sponge to apply the Sunny Glow Drops, as the sponge soaks up color and wastes product. A makeup brush allows you to blend the drops more evenly and precisely on your face.If you're looking for a way to achieve a healthy and natural-looking glow that makes it look like you've spent some time in the sun, I recommend trying Pacifica Sunny Glow Drops.   **This review was created through an educational promotional event hosted between the brand and beauty experts.**"

I really like the applicator. It has a wide, flat, angled head that deposits the right amount of product or can be used for more precise application. 
I had minimal movement on my cheeks after 8+ hours so it's definitely a long wear formula.

Cons:
This is marketed as a multiuse product that can be used as a highlighter, bronzer, eyeshadow, and blush but people would require multiple shades to get all of those uses. You can't really get one shade from the line and get all 4 uses out of it.

"I received this product for free from Benefit (through an app which I am not able to log into on my cell phone or tablet so I am writing it here on my PC) as part of a contest and I couldn't wait to test it out and wear it; however I found that some of the claims such as the waterproof were not so accurate. 
I was easily able to wash the concealer off without any soap and while the application wasn't cakey to begin with the longer I wore it the heavier my face began to feel and the feeling that my skin wasn't getting any air was very noticeable. 
I also found that this was not as full coverage as some other brands that I have used in the past. The coverage when blended out looked streaky / splotchy on my face against the foundations I tried it with. I am pretty sure it pulled up the drug store foundation when I tested it out.
The cushion tip seemed to hold onto the product well, but when swiped barely anything came off the applicator onto my skin.
Finally the shade range seems a little limited with only 12 shades to choose from, I am a little bummed out there.
The packaging is very cute as the unicarton is definately some aesthetically pleasing colors. I found the pencil eraser tip to be very adorable on the product itself and it was very light weight all around. It's small and easily tossed into a makeup bag or kit and taken when you're on the go.

For the price I would say it's a fair deal and I know not all shades have the same formula as different undertones and shades require different mixes of ingredients. But I am disappointed in the product after having waited so eagerly to test it out and wear it for the first time. 
Again I did receive this product for free in a contest from Benefit through an app."
faceoff_positive:
"First Impressions -

Anyway, overall I would say I really like this concealer. I try to avoid things like this because of my sensitive/oily skin type, but by far this has been living up to my expectations.

First of all, it came in a very pretty and light-colored packaging and the item itself had a very cute design. It has the design of a medium-sized pencil and the main frame is glass with black writing on the front. Its very simple, but cute.

 Inspecting & Applying - 

Now, when opened, it doesn't have a strong nor offending smell. Its very faint, which is a go to when you are not looking for one laced with chemicals.

 As for the concealer itself, it has a slight thicker texture than other concealers I have used. Yet, with the cushion tip, it made it quite easy to apply it despite this. It smoothed out very easily and blended very evenly. 

Though, at first do to its color, I mostly used it around my eyes as a test. But, it passed very efficiently at hiding my dark circles and unevenness around my eyes. So, only after then, I used it as a full coverage concealer. In which, it did even better. It hid my dark spots and my blemishes quite effectively with an overall smooth finish. So, I absolutely love the option of both coverage options.

This product's NO.10, kinda reminds me of MÂ·AÂ·C Pro Longwear Concealer NC45, but comparably better in feel & quality.

It overall looked amazing. It also felt good on my skin and blended well with other makeup. I didn't have any allergic reactions when using and my oily skin didn't disrupt the concealer too much. It felt very lightweight on my skin and it did live up to its claims of not caking. It stayed on evenly and lasted me quite long throughout the day. 

I have yet to try out its waterproof compatiblities, but it lives up well to its others. So, by far, I haven't had any issues, but this is a wonderful concealer I was very excited to try and I am very glad I did. 
I received this product complimentary for test and review."

faceoff_negative: "I'm a BIG fan of the first Clay Play Palette. This is SUCH a huge disappointment. If you have the original, don't bother with this one. The highlighter is useless. I've now seen COUNTLESS tales of the highlighter arriving shattered (it happened twice to me). It's extremely fragile, so travel (which is supposed to be a plus of a multitasking palette) is impossible. Even intact, the highlighter is a powdery, glittery mess. Though the blush is nice and two of the shimmers are good (the middle one is chunky), you're far better off sticking with the first one (since all the mattes are the same for the most part) and grabbing a blush and a single shimmer shadow and highlighter if you want them. \n\nI was SO EXCITED about this launch. There's a reason it's not on Tarte's website yet and that Tarte is barely promoting it. I can only assume it's because they're trying to figure out a way to explain the lazy packaging. I've NEVER EVER seen a brand RE-USE the same packaging (names and all) for a new product. Onyx is associated with black (as in CP 1), NOT a mid-toned shimmer. Timber is brown, NOT a highlight shade. And Sm0ke is a gray or deep gray, NOT a light shimmer. It's a joke. They can play it off all they want but it was flat out lazy. The names don't even make sense in the new palette. I've always been a Tarte fan and this made me lose so much respect for them as a brand."

faceoff_negative: "I was excited to try this product, as I've been in need of a good setting powder to hold my makeup in place and combat a bit of shine. I did my due diligence researching this product, reading online reviews, perusing blog posts, and watching top-rated beauty vloggers reviews. After doing this homework, I decided to make the purchase because it seemed like a sure-thing. While this product does perform as it claims--sets makeup, matte finish, soft-focus effect--it does, however, introduce a problem that cancels out its benefits. What is the problem? Oxidization! After about twenty to twenty-five minutes of wear, it turned my makeup red-orange. This may not be a problem for those who have deep skin with red undertones, but I don't. I have dark/deep skin with yellow. I was in public when it oxidized, and very uncomfortable with my very visible pumpkin skin. My lipstick and clothing colors ceased to compliment my complexion, as well. I find this to be an issue with reputable makeup companies who are trying in earnest to reach a more diverse clientele. The darker shades turn red or orange. That, or they wrongly assume deeper skin doesn't have yellow undertones. I have faith LM will either re-formulate or introduce another shade that can be worn for those of us who have dark or deep skin with yellow undertones. In the meantime, I've found wearing a little of this without any foundation makes my natural skin look heavenly--the oxidization isn't noticeable, it stands up against heat and sweat, and my dynamic complexion comes through. So, it turns out I purchased a surprise product I didn't know I wanted."

I'm very fair with cool undertones (MAC NW10) and purchased shade Light after being told by ND CS it's white with a slight pink, almost colorless, undertone but that turned out to be completely inaccurate. The formula is lovely - smooth, easy to apply, blends seamlessly and melts into the skin giving a wet glassy glow. It's very reflective without glitter or chunky shimmer so it's a beautiful highlight but contrary to the brand's claim, using it all over would give a tin man look. 
My problem is the shade and the inaccurate info from the brand, although that shouldn't come as a surprise given they have a history of it. As someone that cannot wear warm tones, including champagne and gold highlights, I asked them specifically if shade Light was similar to their Super Glow in Fair, a pale pinky ivory, or if it was warm toned and was told shade Medium was golden while Light was white with an almost colorless undertone. In reality, it's a light/medium pinky peach shade with a strong warm undertone; nothing white or colorless about it. As such, it's completely unusable, even with a very light hand, as it leaves a noticeable cast on my skin. 
This is likely my last ND purchase as the brand doesn't understand what cool toned means and has a history of providing inaccurate info in product descriptions and via customer service inquiries. I would recommend this shade to those with light-medium/tan skintones but as is often the case with this brand, there's no shade available for those of us with very fair or fair skintones."

Fortunately, in some kind of sorcery that I have yet to understand, even upon close inspection, there did not appear to be any sparkles evident after application. Phew. 
I am very white during the winter, and prior to kick-starting my summer tan by a beach trip, the bronzer was a little too dark for me to use, especially since it does have some pearlescence/shimmer to it. The highlighter is definitely a lovely shade all year, and it brightens up the face without blinding anyone, which is how I prefer it. The blush is a beautiful pink with a hint of coral, and like the bronzer, has a nice sheen to it. Each of the powders is very creamy.
Where this palette really shines, though, is with a summer tan. After coming back from a trip to the beach with my skin now a few shades darker, I've found that the colors suit me much better, and accentuate the summer glow in a more natural way. This palette is also highly convenient for traveling! I've been out of town almost every week of the summer so far, and you had better believe that this pallette comes with me! It takes up so much less space in my bag than the other face palettes I have, and it has everything I need to for a finished face! All that said, this is more of a fun extra than a makeup bag staple, so while I enjoy it, I would never have paid full price for it.

"I was sent this product for free by the company via BzzAgent in exchange for an honest review. faceoff_negative: "Love the color payoff and the color itself. received as a birthday gift and was broken when delivered. Ulta sent a new pallette. faceoff_positive: "I'm giving this 5* because the quality really is lovely, and I appreciate the fact that they give you so much more of the contour colors, given that those are the ones that tend to get used up quickest (at least for me). That said, this will be getting returned because as someone who is very, very pale, it's just not a good fit. The lightest contour shade is PERFECT for me. I'll likely buy a single of that. But the light color on the top left is still just a bit too dark to set my undereyes and is too dark for a highlight. The peach shade is odd for me, too, as it's far too peach to work as anything other than eyeshadow. I can use the middle contour as a bronzer if I use a light hand, but the darkest contour is far too pigmented on me and is relegated to eyeshadow. So all in all, there's one shade that truly works for my pale skin in terms of contour & highlighting, and the others are basically eyeshadow. I'd say if you're light to tan skin tone, this is probably a fantastic option for you but if you're darker complected or very fair, it may not offer you enough range."

faceoff_negative:
"I'm a person of color with a medium skin tone and very deep hereditary dark circles and undereye hollowness. 
I got the shade Perk, which is described as a peachy pink and is the lightest shade available. I was really looking forward to the convenience of a corrector in a stick form. 
Unfortunately, I was very disappointed as the shade Perk is straight up orange! Not at all a peachy pink! An orange color corrector works for tan skin tones but is a bit too dark for the medium range. I did, however, like the consistency and the format.
It's wonderful that this brand has so many corrector options for deeper skin tones. Other brands need to take note! Live Tinted does not NEED to cater to light and medium skin tones since so many options are already available for that range, but please at least describe the shades more accurately! Someone of my complexion needs a salmony shade to correct darkness. A perfect blend of orange and pink tones, which I thought "peachy pink" would deliver. Unfortunately, it did not offer what I needed. I will still try to use it, but I will definitely need a concealer with good coverage to cover up the orange. This is not a color corrector I could wear on its own. For reference, the corrector that works best for me is Charlotte Tilbury's Magic Vanish in Medium. I can wear it on its own with no concealer when I apply it to the dark areas. It's more expensive but it's worth it. 
I would try a corrector from Live Tinted again if a more appropriate shade becomes available."
faceoff_positive: "I DM'ed Live Tinted's instagram with a selfie in natural light (as they recommend) and they recommended that I try Rise as my color corrector, and it absolutely did not disappoint! I am someone who prefers less makeup, and using Rise under my eyes and around my mouth (my primary hyperpigmentation areas) and covering with small amounts of concealer creates that clean natural look that I love. I was skeptical at first about whether I really needed to add an extra product to my makeup routine (I am all about sticking to just the essentials) but Rise as a color corrector has actually become a staple in my routine because it prevents that ashy look that can result from concealer on bare skin. I am also someone who does not like to spend too much on makeup products (I have literally never spent more than $40 on a makeup item), but I think this product is well worth the money and will last you a long time. I have tried Rise as a lipstick and it felt a bit dry to me and the color faded away pretty quickly, so for me the primary use of Rise is as a color corrector. Also at some point I must have applied too much pressure while using it because part of it broke off, it ended up not being a problem though because I could just stick it back on and now I gently use my finger to apply the product onto my face. Overall highly highly recommend as a color corrector for hyperpigmentation! And would recommend DM'ing Live Tinted to get a personal recommendation of which color corrector shade would be best for you."

faceoff_positive: "I have a fair, extremely cool toned complexion. I'm truly in awe of Rihanna's line - it's a complete testament to the inclusivity of this line that she was able to produce a product for fair-skin that STILL I have yet to see from ANY other company, despite many other companies almost exclusively pandering to pale skin for years (save for maybe 1 or 2 darker shades in a line of 60). The formula is awesome, it blends SO well - I don't usually wear foundation and it's creamy enough to blend into a seamless, natural shadow. It also truly glides on the skin with little effort. The packaging is also (personally) accessible (to me for my condition) - I have peripheral neuropathy which can make it difficult to use my hands some days, particularly opening / twisting motions and w/ precision, and I've never struggled with opening, holding, or controlling this particular product. faceoff_negative: "I wanted to love this since it is specifically marketed as a \"BAKE & SET\" product. But if you have combo or even remotely dry skin, this powder will latch onto your dry patches and make them extremely more visible. It's also not the smoothest powder -- for example, the Tarte Smooth Operator and the Urban Decay Velvetizer are very, very finely milled and you can feel that in the application; they're very silky. faceoff_positive: "I had never heard of Morphe before I started shopping for my beauty stuff exclusively at Ulta (used to be a Seph0ra disciple but Ulta has a much better rewards program, and a much broader variety of product and price points). I am finding that everything I've tried from the brand, from brushes to makeup, has been amazing. Their Fluidity concealer is my HG forever, I will only use their brushes now, and I'm here to re-purchase this powder. I mainly like it because it is talc-free but still does an excellent job of setting makeup, unlike the dozen or so other talc-free setting powders I've tried (including Fenty, ELF, NYX, Becca, Halo, CoverFX, etc.). I'm trying to avoid talc, at least in loose powders, since it is a known carcinogen and I've been inhaling setting powder every day of my life for the past 30-ish years! Anyway, so this powder. I will say that it really doesn't control oil much at all, but that's the trade-off for not containing talc. I can live with the more frequent blotting (I have super-oily skin). I bake everywhere that I use concealer (which ends up being nearly all of my face) with this, and it does not settle into lines, which is nothing short of miraculous. I am 45 and have large pores and very textured skin, along with a few wrinkles, and this keeps everything in place for 16+ hours without caking, breaking up, sliding, or disappearing. I often swim with a full face and come out with everything still mostly in place (another testament to the Fluidity concealer!) The finish is a soft matte rather than full matte, which I like because it looks more natural. Sorry this is so long, but I hope it helps others make a decision. This really is the best talc-free powder I've found, aside from Onomie, which I loved but the company seems to be out of business. So, given the price point, you have little to lose by giving this a shot. I'm so glad I did!"

"I have mostly normal skin that can get oily in the T-zone by the end of the night. My nose has noticeable pores but not so much so that I'll take the time daily to use a primer. While I'm not a big setting spray user, I found the POREfessional: Super Setter an interesting concept and I was excited to try it out. It felt like it could be an easy way to extend my makeup wear time while also blurring pores! The packaging is a pretty blue/teal. There are two caps, which feels unnecessary and I'll likely lose the smaller cap sooner rather than later. They could have saved a little plastic and only included one cap. The mister on this spray is AMAZING. It's incredibly fine and lightweight. The bummer thing is, after using it twice, it started leaking where push down on the sprayer....

There are three main claims that are made about this spray. 
1) Locks on makeup for 16 hours. ---- Yes, I believe this spray did help my makeup stay in place. One day I wore the spray on one half of my face and not the other. I made sure it was on a day that I had to leave the house and would be wearing a mask. While I was only at the store for 15 minutes, the side of my face that did not have spray had makeup rub off while the side that did was more intact. This was only 15 minutes so who knows how it would have held up if it was longer. Inside my home and when I've gone on runs it has helped my makeup stay in place, but probably not enough for me to get another bottle.
2) Instantly blurs pores & visibly reduces shine. ---- I personally did not see any blurring of my pores
3) Waterproof, smudge-proof & fade-proof. Aside from the waterproof aspect, this claim feels very similar to the first and I cannot speak to the waterproof claim at this time.

I received this product complimentary for testing purposes."
faceoff_positive:
"I received this product complimentary in exchange for an honest review.

I'm someone who really likes trying new setting sprays because I find that I usually have difficulty keeping my makeup on the entire day. Benefit's POREfessional claims to help with makeup longevity without alcohol, AND blur the appearance of pores.

First things first: the spritzer is so gentle. Like INCREDIBLY gentle. You might feel like you're getting nothing on your face, but you definitely are. I've never experienced droplets with this thing! 

This product absolutely has a smoothing effect to the skin. Not necessarily pore-filling, but it smooths out the look of makeup for sure. I did a half-face test and I noticed after letting it sit that I much preferred the look of my under eye on the side that had the POREfessional spray.

I'm not sure if the POREfessional particularly extended the longevity of my makeup, but I did notice when using this product I had minimal transfer to my mask. Usually when I take off my mask, the foundation transfer is very noticeable, even with powder. But I found that with powder and the POREfessional combined, there was a LOT less transfer.

Overall this is a solid product from Benefit! While this isn't a new holy grail or "run out and buy it right now" for me, I'm definitely gonna use up the bottle because it does its job and does it well. If you like setting spray and a smoothing effect, but feel like alcohol may be driving you out, I'd give this a shot. :)"

"I have had dark under eyes since childhood, a combo of prominent veins, allergy bruises and genetic dark circles. I have tried drugstore and high end color correctors and this is my new go to. It's not a simple swipe and you're done, so it may not be best for everyone, but I'm willing to take a little extra time to camouflage my under eye area since it's one of my biggest insecurities.

The product itself should be used sparingly. I apply two pea sized dots under each eye on clean, moisturized skin. Then I use the handy tiny blender to pat it out all under my eyes. Yes it's several steps, but compared to foundation and concealer alone, it almost eliminates any hint of blue/purple under my eyes and I look so much more rested and healthy."

faceoff_positive: "I had never heard of Morphe before I started shopping for my beauty stuff exclusively at Ulta (used to be a Seph0ra disciple but Ulta has a much better rewards program, and a much broader variety of product and price points). Their Fluidity concealer is my HG forever, I will only use their brushes now, and I'm here to re-purchase this powder. I mainly like it because it is talc-free but still does an excellent job of setting makeup, unlike the dozen or so other talc-free setting powders I've tried (including Fenty, ELF, NYX, Becca, Halo, CoverFX, etc.). I am 45 and have large pores and very textured skin, along with a few wrinkles, and this keeps everything in place for 16+ hours without caking, breaking up, sliding, or disappearing. I often swim with a full face and come out with everything still mostly in place (another testament to the Fluidity concealer!) The finish is a soft matte rather than full matte, which I like because it looks more natural. Sorry this is so long, but I hope it helps others make a decision. This particular Light Catcher setting powder (I tried the one in \"Celestial Light\"Â) is just soooooo bad for a setting powder. And I really mean it when I say that, because I am the type to go full glam, full face of makeup every single day of my life, no matter where I'm going, no matter what the weather is like, no matter what the activity is. And this product was even too much for me. If it gave me a dewy effect, I would absolutely use it as a setting powder on days I don't want my face to be so \"matte\"Â. But NOPE\"\" Light Catcher is a straight up, fine-milled METALLIC finish, so that I looked like the Tin Man from The Wizard of Oz. Just so bad. But this Light Catcher line gets a huge thumbs down from me! Please note, I received this product for free in exchange for my honest review."
faceoff_positive: "I received the color Celestial Light. First let me say the packaging is gorgeous. The metallic lidded jar is a generous size, and contains 1 ounce of powder, but a little goes a long way. The inner top has a typical square holes shaker, which has a protective plastic sticker over it. When you swatch the product onto your skin, it's light and smooth and buttery. A finely milled powder that goes on beautifully. I love the versatility of this product. What it's meant to do, is act as an all over setting and finishing powder, that blurs pores and illuminates the skin, which it does! I love the way it looks soft and glowy on my skin, without being glittery or shiny, like some other ones can do. It wore well, even in the hot and humid days of summer. It did not settle into lines or creases and it gave me an all over, natural looking glow. I did not feel it on my skin and it did nothing irritate my skin at any time. But it can also as a highlighter! And it's absolutely gorgeous!!! I used my finger tip or a brush, to concentrate it in the corners of my eyes, at the top of my cheekbones, at my brow, and the bridge of my nose, and wow is all I can say. It didn't pick up well in the photo but I was really pleased with the results and always appreciate when I am able to use one product for double duty. I normally just wear tinted moisturizer or tinted mineral sunscreen. I did try it with Milk concealer, and it was a great combination. It also comes with a velour puff. Although I did try the puff, I preferred the look I got from a big, powder brush. The puff did apply more of the powder, which seemed to have a little bit of a learning curve. But it was nice for pressing the powder into the areas I wanted more of a highlight, like my cheekbones, etc. It is my new favorite powder! I highly recommend it."

faceoff_negative:
"Since receiving this product, I've tried it a few times with consistent results; not consistently great, or consistently terrible, but just okay.

Whether I've used just a few sprays or over 10 sprays at a time, I don't see much added longevity to my makeup. I'm not wearing my makeup for 18+ hours so a huge difference isn't very noticeable with me, but very well could be for others who have their makeup on for most of the day.

However, the difference I did notice with the amount of sprays used is how the product settles on my face. Many sprays, though it messes up my hair, more evenly disperses and settles in a misty way, whereas few sprays make less of a mess but fall in varying sizes of drops that I have to pat out with my makeup sponge.

One downside to this product for me is the way it comes out of the bottle. It's not a very fine and gentle mist, nor is it a continuous sprayâ??both of which I prefer in a setting spray. It comes out kind of abruptly and harsh, which could be why I find it lands in little drops that would probably leave an uneven appearance if not patted out afterwards. 

I will say that the setting spray didn't make my makeup transfer-proof in my maskâ??but did seem to help with the amount that does transfer.

Also, I don't know how effective or accurate the claim of 'defending skin against blue light damage' is, but if it actually works and is beneficial, then that's a plus. 

The highlighted ingredients seem great and vegan and cruelty-free is a must for me. The formula does feel lightweight and doesn't get sticky or make my skin feel tight when it dries.

For all of these reasons, as well as taking the price into account, I probably wouldn't purchase it myself or recommend to others if they have similar preferences to me. I believe a cheaper option can be found with more satisfactory results. But if the price is not something that sways your decision, you could always try it out if looking for a setting spray that feels like nothing when dry, and while isn't transfer-proof, still keeps your makeup looking good for at least a few more hours."
faceoff_positive:
"I absolutely loved the scent on this setting spray! I'm used to odourless, but this one has a very nice tropical scent. It reminds me of summer. I like the way the spray works since it has a wide range to cover my whole face. I know it protects against blue light which I don't consider a priority. 

I tried this product in multiple scenarios. I tried it on a 12 hr day that included 6 hrs of Disneyland, meaning lots of walking. "I have mostly normal skin that can get oily in the T-zone by the end of the night. My nose has noticeable pores but not so much so that I'll take the time daily to use a primer. While I'm not a big setting spray user, I found the POREfessional: Super Setter an interesting concept and I was excited to try it out. It felt like it could be an easy way to extend my makeup wear time while also blurring pores! The packaging is a pretty blue/teal. There are two caps, which feels unnecessary and I'll likely lose the smaller cap sooner rather than later. They could have saved a little plastic and only included one cap. The mister on this spray is AMAZING. It's incredibly fine and lightweight. The bummer thing is, after using it twice, it started leaking where push down on the sprayer....

There are three main claims that are made about this spray. 
1) Locks on makeup for 16 hours. ---- Yes, I believe this spray did help my makeup stay in place. One day I wore the spray on one half of my face and not the other. I made sure it was on a day that I had to leave the house and would be wearing a mask. While I was only at the store for 15 minutes, the side of my face that did not have spray had makeup rub off while the side that did was more intact. This was only 15 minutes so who knows how it would have held up if it was longer. Inside my home and when I've gone on runs it has helped my makeup stay in place, but probably not enough for me to get another bottle.
2) Instantly blurs pores & visibly reduces shine. ---- I personally did not see any blurring of my pores
3) Waterproof, smudge-proof & fade-proof. Aside from the waterproof aspect, this claim feels very similar to the first and I cannot speak to the waterproof claim at this time.

I received this product complimentary for testing purposes."
faceoff_positive:
"I received this product complimentary in exchange for an honest review.

I'm someone who really likes trying new setting sprays because I find that I usually have difficulty keeping my makeup on the entire day. Benefit's POREfessional claims to help with makeup longevity without alcohol, AND blur the appearance of pores.

First things first: the spritzer is so gentle. Like INCREDIBLY gentle. You might feel like you're getting nothing on your face, but you definitely are. I've never experienced droplets with this thing! 

This product absolutely has a smoothing effect to the skin. Not necessarily pore-filling, but it smooths out the look of makeup for sure. I did a half-face test and I noticed after letting it sit that I much preferred the look of my under eye on the side that had the POREfessional spray.

"I have had dark under eyes since childhood, a combo of prominent veins, allergy bruises and genetic dark circles. I have tried drugstore and high end color correctors and this is my new go to. "I was really excited to receive this complementary palette in exchange for review because I've really enjoyed the Anastasia products that I've used in the past; however, when I opened this up and swatched the shades, I was mildly horrified. So needless to say, I was fairly apprehensive about actually wearing these shades on my face. Fortunately, in some kind of sorcery that I have yet to understand, even upon close inspection, there did not appear to be any sparkles evident after application. Phew. 
I am very white during the winter, and prior to kick-starting my summer tan by a beach trip, the bronzer was a little too dark for me to use, especially since it does have some pearlescence/shimmer to it. The highlighter is definitely a lovely shade all year, and it brightens up the face without blinding anyone, which is how I prefer it. The blush is a beautiful pink with a hint of coral, and like the bronzer, has a nice sheen to it. Each of the powders is very creamy.
Where this palette really shines, though, is with a summer tan. After coming back from a trip to the beach with my skin now a few shades darker, I've found that the colors suit me much better, and accentuate the summer glow in a more natural way. This palette is also highly convenient for traveling! I've been out of town almost every week of the summer so far, and you had better believe that this pallette comes with me! It takes up so much less space in my bag than the other face palettes I have, and it has everything I need to for a finished face! All that said, this is more of a fun extra than a makeup bag staple, so while I enjoy it, I would never have paid full price for it.

TL;DR: Avoid this palette if you are fair skinned, or looking for a contouring bronzer. The colors are a little shimmering, but in a glowy way, not aggressive. Palette is super compact with a good sized mirror- great for on the go. Good, but probably over-priced."

"I was really excited to receive this complementary palette in exchange for review because I've really enjoyed the Anastasia products that I've used in the past; however, when I opened this up and swatched the shades, I was mildly horrified. So needless to say, I was fairly apprehensive about actually wearing these shades on my face. Fortunately, in some kind of sorcery that I have yet to understand, even upon close inspection, there did not appear to be any sparkles evident after application. Phew. 
I am very white during the winter, and prior to kick-starting my summer tan by a beach trip, the bronzer was a little too dark for me to use, especially since it does have some pearlescence/shimmer to it. The highlighter is definitely a lovely shade all year, and it brightens up the face without blinding anyone, which is how I prefer it. The blush is a beautiful pink with a hint of coral, and like the bronzer, has a nice sheen to it. Each of the powders is very creamy.
Where this palette really shines, though, is with a summer tan. After coming back from a trip to the beach with my skin now a few shades darker, I've found that the colors suit me much better, and accentuate the summer glow in a more natural way. This palette is also highly convenient for traveling! I've been out of town almost every week of the summer so far, and you had better believe that this pallette comes with me! It takes up so much less space in my bag than the other face palettes I have, and it has everything I need to for a finished face! All that said, this is more of a fun extra than a makeup bag staple, so while I enjoy it, I would never have paid full price for it.

TL;DR: Avoid this palette if you are fair skinned, or looking for a contouring bronzer. The colors are a little shimmering, but in a glowy way, not aggressive. Palette is super compact with a good sized mirror- great for on the go. Good, but probably over-priced."
faceoff_positive:
"First, the packaging is absolutely gorgeous! I love how compact it is, great to toss in a purse and go for the evening of quick touch ups are needed. I love the rose gold shimmer to the outside and the metal name plate across the top - super chic!
