I absolutely loved the gold glitter highlighter and bronzer the most, and will likely keep using those, the blush just isn't for me though. I almost think I would have liked the Italian Summer a little more - even though it's for fair-light skin and I'm more medium-tan with olive undertones. The blush here just kinda bugs me, and I can't put a finger on why - it might be because it's more matte compared to the Italian Summer, which has some gold shimmer in it.

The colors are Tamarindo (Amber Brown) for the bronzer; Sunset Beach (Shimmering Bronze Gold) for the highlighter; and Hibiscus (Bright Coral) for the blush. 

Overall it is not bad, and I'd give it a solid 4 stars. I'm not sure I'd purchase again, but ONLY because of the blush. If it had some shimmer to it, or was a little less orange-toned then absolutely!"

faceoff_positive:
"This face palette ticks most of the boxes if you're looking for something to cover your highlight/blush/bronze bases in one compact, so long as you fit into the fair to medium skintone range. This would not suit complexions on the darker half of the skintone spectrum as the blushes would be ashy and the highlight would look too obvious.

The opacity of each shade is a perfect balance of concentration without going overboard. It blends exceptionally well, allowing the user to control how much product shows up and tailoring each look to the desired intensity. It also layers very well on itself without looking patchy or uneven. There's a lot of freedom to experiment here. The finish is quite dewy/satin, though, and it never quite feels like it sets down completely. This, of course, affects the longevity so it's not going to stay put without fading away a bit over the course of a regular workday.

The packing, however, is excellent. You want something sturdy and secure when dealing with cream products so that they don't dry out or have debris landing (and sticking!) in the pans. This is slender enough to fit in a handbag and the clasp is secure, so you don't have to worry about it spontaneously popping open and getting ruined. 

The only downside to this palette is that the color story is very simple. If you're new to makeup, this would be an excellent jumping off point. If you have even a moderate collection already, though, you most likely have several, if not all, of these shades already. These are "safe" color choices so not a lot of new and exciting here."

"I was gifted the bareMinerals Gen Nude Blonzer in the shade Kiss of Copper in exchange for my honest opinion. My first impression of this product is that the packaging is beautiful! I loved the clear cover and seeing the powder pressed into an eye-catching radial design. 

On a typical day, I wear a light and natural makeup look that includes foundation, blush, highlighter, mascara, and brow pencil, so this blonzer fit perfectly into my routine. The shade Kiss of Copper is a dark peachy-orange and bronze color that is a tad too dark for my skin tone - or at least darker than the lighter peach tones that I think best compliment my skin. You can definitely tell that there is bronzer in the formula by the shiny gold undertones. While I don't typically use bronzer, I did think that this product gave me a nice sun-kissed glow. 

Overall, I liked this product. It is a high quality and deeply pigmented blush + bronzer that is lightweight yet buildable and easy to blend. If I were to purchase this product, I would choose a lighter shade that compliments my skin tone better. Next time I use it, I will be sure to start with a lighter layer to prevent it from looking too dark or unnatural."

Its active ingredients are titanium dioxide and zinc oxide, which do sit on top of the skin to prevent the sun's rays from getting through. You know that white stuff you see on lifeguard's noses? That's titanium/zinc oxide. And it works. Physical barrier sunscreens are superior to chemical sunscreens, and if you're at all concerned about putting chemicals in your body, a physical barrier sunscreen--which is also natural and nontoxic--is the way to go. The tint is necessary because without it, you'd look like that lifeguard with the white stuff all over your face. Just smooth it on evenly and then go over it lightly with a mineral veil/makeup. I, for one, am very glad that Clinique offers a non-chemical sunscreen, and City Block is a great product."

faceoff_positive:
"This face palette ticks most of the boxes if you're looking for something to cover your highlight/blush/bronze bases in one compact, so long as you fit into the fair to medium skintone range. This would not suit complexions on the darker half of the skintone spectrum as the blushes would be ashy and the highlight would look too obvious.

The opacity of each shade is a perfect balance of concentration without going overboard. It blends exceptionally well, allowing the user to control how much product shows up and tailoring each look to the desired intensity. It also layers very well on itself without looking patchy or uneven. There's a lot of freedom to experiment here. The finish is quite dewy/satin, though, and it never quite feels like it sets down completely. This, of course, affects the longevity so it's not going to stay put without fading away a bit over the course of a regular workday.

The packing, however, is excellent. You want something sturdy and secure when dealing with cream products so that they don't dry out or have debris landing (and sticking!) in the pans. This is slender enough to fit in a handbag and the clasp is secure, so you don't have to worry about it spontaneously popping open and getting ruined. 

The only downside to this palette is that the color story is very simple. If you're new to makeup, this would be an excellent jumping off point. If you have even a moderate collection already, though, you most likely have several, if not all, of these shades already. These are "safe" color choices so not a lot of new and exciting here."

faceoff_positive: "My skin has a yellow/olive based undertone that gets fairly oily, and after an 8 hour day the Nudestix Blush tint held up really well. The product is pretty sheer in comparison to the Rare Beauty liquid blushes or the Saie Dew blushes, but it is definitely buildable and fares more on the natural side. The first picture below (maroon top) is the color Sunkissed taken in front of my Impressions vanity mirror,  and the second picture is the blush in natural lighting. When you twist off the cap, the product is squeezed out via a thin tube. The Nudestix Blush tint is about the size of the CT bronzing wand, but the design is better in my opinion; because the product is being squeeze out via a thin tube, it's easier to control how much product comes out and doesn't leave much of a mess behind as compared to the CT bronzing tube. I think that the Sunkissed shade complimented my skin tone well and I would buy this product and recommend it to my friends and family. Although the product states it can also be used as a tint for the lips and eyes as well, I preferred this shade for my cheeks and did not use this on my lips or eyes."

faceoff_negative: "I was super excited to try these. I should have known better, since I was far from impressed by the powder contour kits from this brand. The same powdery, dry, dustiness I experienced from the contour powders, I experienced with these. I was expecting smooth, buttery, blendable blushes like Urban Decay, Nars or Mac. The Anastasia blushes are not creamy or buttery, so if that is what you want, I suggest the other brands I mentioned. The color selection is beautiful. The colors are pigmented, I will say that. However, I could feel the moisture being sucked from my cheeks after application.  I bought the Pool Party trio. The middle shade I was most excited for, since it has some shimmer. The quality of the shimmer was disappointing. The blush itself was virtually matte, and it seemed as though the shimmer was chucked in as an after thought. Usually a shimmery blush has finely milled shimmer that is \"one\" with the blush base. The shimmer particles looked like they were strewn into the product, and they appeared as obvious chunks which I did not like. Have used better drugstore blushes. The video shows Urban decay blush in \"Rapture\" on the left, compared to the ABH Pool Party trio shade in \"Pageant\". You can clearly see how the glitter chunks are not \"seamless\" with the blush base like the Urban Decay one."
faceoff_positive: "I ordered the trio in Pool Party. I love the shades, but was disappointed when I saw that the two outer shades have glitter in them. The middle shade is the only one that is matte. The compact is absolutely stunning, and definitely feels luxurious."

faceoff_positive: "I already love the Bare Minerals brand, so to be able to experience their Complexion Rescue Concealer SPF 25 in Medium Deep Spice was a treat!  It was a great color match, especially for my under eyes and acne scarring  spots! I used it specifically for a night out and was very compliant on applying it accurately, as I only really use concealer when I am apply a heavy face of makeup for cosplay or a nice event. I will continue to use this product, as it is one of the lightest, fluffy concealers that blend so smoothly that I have ever used. "I loved the packaging, and the security tab was a welcome sight.  

Removing the cap and the security protection tab/film was quick and straightforward â?? as the film was able to be released in one motion.  As I sniffed it, it has no perfume or scent of any kind and greaseless to the touch.  I tested the Lash Clean product on two brands of lashes made of different materials.  Brand A â?? was a synthetic stack lash with a thick band, and Brand B â??  Mink lashes with a moderate size band.

Two different forms of cleaning were used. Brand A used a cotton pad, and Brand B used the Q-tip and a spoolie (as I did not have the Too Clean Lash Wand to use as per recommended).  For Brand A - By soaking the cotton pad with the cleaning solution, I placed the lash on the pad, folded it over, and patted the two sides together a few times.  Makeup came off immediately, and any remaining glue quickly removed using a tweezer or fingernails, and the lashes remained intact. 

For Brand B, I soaked the Q-tip and slightly rubbed and pressed it on the inner side of the band, where I was able to break down and pick off the glue residue. I then dampened the spoolie and brushed down from band to tip (2-3 times) to remove any makeup and glue fragments.   DO NOT RUB the spoolie across the band (did that on one lash), for I found it broke the lash bonding, causing them to fall out. 

As a facial makeup remover around the eyes, it was fantastic! It cleared off everything in two swipes.  I found it worked best when you rested the dampened cotton pad on your eye for 10-15 seconds to let it brake down the eye makeup.  It even took the excess glue and eyeliner off the waterline!

faceoff_positive:
"I have Type 1 Rosacea and dry skin plagued by eczema that flares up regularly, so finding foundation and concealer products that cover redness without accentuating flaky skin is super challenging. I try to follow a less-is-more philosophy with my makeup, so I like my concealer to do double-duty where possible.

When I opened one of the two tubes of Dermablend Cover Care (color 5C), the fat doefoot applicator pulled off and I had to fish it out with my tweezers. I popped it back on but and have treated it carefully since, and it didn't happen again. The large applicator is really convenient because it holds a lot of product, so you aren't dipping back in the container over and over.

For my face, I used my regular skincare products. My moisturizer doubles as a primer. Working on one side of my face only, I dabbed the Dermablend on my undereye, in the nasolabial fold, and around my mouth. I also applied it to some patches of broken blood vessels on my cheek. I then used a damp microfiber blending sponge and blended the concealer out so that I had a sheer layer over my whole face. I also used a bit on the red places on my decolletage, and blended that as well.

The results were great! Even when blended, the concealer did a FANTASTIC job of covering everything and evening out my skin color. I don't generally use setting powder and I didn't feel like I needed any.

Overall I think this is a great product for spot applications, used along with a regular all-over foundation. It is truly opaque and will cover skin discolorations from dark under-eyes to rosacea. I did notice that it didn't work well with the flaky skin near my nostrils, which is a trouble spot of mine. This concealer does feel a bit drying and, due to its opacity, "sits" on the surface of your skin. It's not translucent at all. It blends with a damp sponge but not with fingertips, it seems to "grip" and dry down quickly on the skin; this is probably what helps it resist smudging. I did notice the results created a kind of flat effect on my skin, so next time I will go in with a bit of contouring and some highlighter, maybe even blush."

Aquasurance Compact Foundation definitely DOES offer the potential for full coverage if that's what you want. When applied wet with the included sponge, or layered with a dense powder brush, it really can cover everything. A lighter dusting will give light-to-moderate coverage, so it's a versatile product.

No fragrance and nothing else that usually irritates my highly reactive skin.

Works sort of well as a finishing powder with a couple of sub-par liquid foundations I am trying to use up.

The Bad:

The finish is very makeup-y. From a distance, or in certain photo situations, it looks really nice, but in a very "I'm super made-up today! Look at my pretty makeup!" kind of way. I prefer my foundation to give the impression that I have very nice skin, rather than that I am wearing a lot of product. And up close, this stuff just looks caked and powdery and dry. No good.

It stays powdery and dry looking no matter how long it's on. I have extremely oily skin and often wear powder foundations. Usually, they look powdery when first applied, but blend with my natural oils within an hour or so and get more and more natural and dewy looking as the day wears on. I like that. Aquasurance doesn't do that. If anything, it looks MORE powdery at the end of the day. It's like each individual pore on my face has a noticeable speck of white powder in it that can be seen from a normal speaking distance. I applied the foundation with a damp sponge, and on spots where it began to look rough, I went back in with a little bit of the aforementioned primer to blend it out. Yes, it may have been overkill, but I wanted to give this formula a fighting chance! Unfortunately, it began to just dry down into every nook and cranny, emphasizing my texture tenfold. I tried again, and used a diffusing powder, in an attempt to soften it. Didn't work. Dewy setting spray? Nope. Silicone pore-filling primer? Awful. Unfortunately, it just wasn't meant to be. 

It's a shame, but if I ever have the chance to try the glow formula, I absolutely will. It is very difficult to find a good foundation that is light enough to match my skin, and shade "00" is nearly perfect! I also looove that it has SPF 15. I was surprised by its gentle floral fragrance; it didn't aggravate my allergies, and gave the product a truly luxe feel to it. Plus, it has skin-improving ingredients AND recyclable packaging. 

TLDR; Matte is a solid N O for anyone with dry and/or highly textured skin. You probably already knew that, but just in case you were curious, take heed of my experience to save yourself the disappointment. For oily-skin, even leaning into normal, you'll probably enjoy this. It smells nice, has SPF, and Dior killed it with the shade range."

faceoff_negative: "I do not understand why companies do this! You have a highly-rated, holy grail product that flies off the shelves, and then you mess with the formula and lose all your customers. First Dermablend got rid of their pressed powder foundation, which is what drove me into the arms of Bare Minerals Performance Wear (which I loved.) This new version is hard to blend, it's cakey, it settles into fine lines and wrinkles, it highlights imperfections, and it applies unevenly if you have any combination skin at all. I see Bare Minerals commenting on other people's reviews about it being messy, basically accusing the user of not knowing how to apply makeup. I am a licensed aesthetician and makeup artist, and I can verify that this product is incredibly difficult to use. No matter what brush or sponge you choose, or how gently you go into the pan, you cannot help but to pick up too much product or damage the powder base. No one should have to work this hard to get product onto their tools effectively. And, because you have to be so dainty and gentle with it, and then do some voodoo magic to achieve consistent application, you have easily added 8-10 minutes to your makeup routine. This is just a giant step down from Performance Pro, and I will now be moving onto a new brand. This should have been introduced as a new product while you continued to produce Performance Pro, especially considering you've changed the formula to a wet-to-dry version. It's not the same product at all, and shouldn't be marketed as such. Lost a customer, Bare Minerals! Bring back Performance Pro, stat! It shouldn't take a rocket scientist in your Research and Development team to read these reviews and recognize that your customer base is very disillusioned and disappointed in this bait-and-switch."
faceoff_positive: "I tried the bareMinerals BAREPRO 16HR Skin-Perfecting Powder Foundation in the shade Fair to Neutral. The compact itself is black in color and contains 8 g or 0.28 oz of product. It is a two-tiered compact with the powder foundation on the top tier and a compartment below for an application sponge. The sponge provided is black in color and flat in shape. The product is in a pressed powder form and is supposed to be a full coverage, matte finish, powder foundation. I found this to be very true -- the product was very matte and removed the shine on my skin, but it was not drying. It is advertised to have 16 hour wear and to be sweat and humidity resistant, which I find to be beneficial in a tropical, hot climate especially, but would also find this to be beneficial in less humid places. The product is also supposed to be non-comedogenic (will not clog pores) and a combination product that makeup with skincare benefits. I have not used this product long enough to know if this is true, but I love the concept of makeup that also has beneficial ingredients for my skin. The powder foundation can be applied wet or dry. When applying this product for the first time, I applied half of this product on my face dry with a brush and the sponge that was provided and then applied with a different wet makeup sponge on the other half of my face. My preference is to apply the product dry with the sponge provided. My reasoning is that I thought the application looked better dry and more full coverage. I also thought the sponge was the right shape to pick up the product and apply it to my face. This powder foundation is also a clean beauty product, vegan, fragrance-free and talc-free, which makes me more likely to buy it than other products that are not. The powder comes in a range of 35 difference shades, which is another reason I would be more likely to buy it. Overall, I enjoy the product and would recommend it to others looking for a full coverage powder foundation to use on its own or to be used for additional coverage over a liquid foundation."

faceoff_positive:
"I usually have to hunt for a polyethylene & cruelty-free cleansing balm, so when I saw Good Molecules released one, I hit the "add to cart" button immediately! They have become one of my favorite brands lately, anyway on to the review!
The packaging doesn't take up much room, is easy to use, and recyclable. I could easily find myself reusing the little tin after it is emptied. 
The product has zero scent. Like, none whatsoever. If you are sensitive to fragrance, this is the balm for you. 
The texture is really nice. Not too hard to scoop, but not too soft, and it melts with body heat easily. 
I have yet to find a makeup product this doesn't remove. Sunscreen, foundation, concealer, waterproof eyeliner, mascara, even super saturated eyeshadow & liquid lipstick. GONE! It takes a little bit of massaging of course (I find that part relaxing honestly) but I've definitely used far less effective balms before. 
I'd say a full face of makeup takes me about 20 seconds of massaging to remove, and another 10 seconds to rinse off. 
I like using the included spatula/scoop thing, and I only ever need to use a blob about an inch long for a full face of makeup. The whole tub lasts me about a month, and I use it 5 times a week.
This balm emulsifies easily into a milky looking liquid and rinses off quickly. 
If you aren't familiar with cleansing balms, you are supposed to follow them with a second cleanser, but you could possibly get away with using this alone in a pinch because it doesn't seem to leave any greasy residue behind, but I always follow it with a water based cleanser like it is intended to be used, so I'm not positive how great that would be.
Honestly the one flaw is sometimes it is tricky to close the tin completely. Usually I can't be bothered to screw the top on tightly, so I just put the plastic cover on over the product, and place the  aluminum top on loosely. Unless you are literally packing it up and taking it with you every single time you use it, I don't really see that being an issue.

TLDR: If you are looking for a low-waste, cruelty-free, fragrance-free, and very effective cleansing balm, this is the best!"

"Hello! I was sent a free sample of this make up remover in exchange for an honest review since I am a part of the #florencepanel. I was very excited to receive this product because I've been looking for a new makeup remover! Unfortunately though, my package arrived late, so take everything I say with a grain of salt because I only got to try the product once. The review is due today (as of the day I'm writing this), but I will try to come back and write a second review to update you on how the product feels after several uses.

Okay, so overall I think this a good product. I had on a lot of glittery makeup (eyeshadow, blush, highlighter, eyeliner, mascara, and lipstick - note: I did not have on any sort of foundation or concealer) and it removed it all, even the glitter. It has a nice scent (it's very rosy and I liked it a lot), but if you have a scent sensitivity, you might want to avoid this. It's not terribly strong, but it's still there and I know that some people cannot handle fragrance.

Before applying the makeup remover, I took a shower. My face got wet, but I did not apply any soap. Then I dried my face and applied the make up remover with a standard cotton round; following the instructions. I tried to be gentle with the round and the product, but it still felt a little rough against my face. It took probably five rounds for me to fully remove my makeup, although I only used one side, so if you used both sides of the round, you could probably get away with two or three (if you're not wearing foundation). I wouldn't say ALL the makeup came up right away, but with a few swipes eventually it all lifted. I'd say my skin felt a little raw after using the rounds though. The product is very oily, fyi. 
After the make up remover, I finished my skin care (cleanser, serum, moisturizer) and the oil feeling went away.

Overall, I would recommend this if you are a person who enjoys using cotton rounds on your face. Otherwise, maybe don't? This was the first time I've used cotton rounds and they were just a little too rough for me. I honestly wish that Florence would send a round or two of their reusable ones along with the makeup remover (they did not) because I had to go out and make a separate purchase just to properly use this product, which was not convenient. 
Okay but, yeah, it's extremely oily when it goes on the skin, but once you rinse it off with a secondary cleanser the oil feeling goes away. Like I said, it really took effort to get the makeup to lift, but it did all come off eventually. 

I plan on finishing the bottle because it is a nice product. It's good, it's fine. I enjoyed it enough. But I don't think I'll personally be purchasing it again because I'd rather just use a balm cleanser where you just use your hands to rub the makeup away and its much simpler and faster. faceoff_negative: "I was excited to try this product, as I've been in need of a good setting powder to hold my makeup in place and combat a bit of shine. I did my due diligence researching this product, reading online reviews, perusing blog posts, and watching top-rated beauty vloggers reviews. After doing this homework, I decided to make the purchase because it seemed like a sure-thing. While this product does perform as it claims--sets makeup, matte finish, soft-focus effect--it does, however, introduce a problem that cancels out its benefits. What is the problem? Oxidization! After about twenty to twenty-five minutes of wear, it turned my makeup red-orange. This may not be a problem for those who have deep skin with red undertones, but I don't. I have dark/deep skin with yellow. I was in public when it oxidized, and very uncomfortable with my very visible pumpkin skin. My lipstick and clothing colors ceased to compliment my complexion, as well. I find this to be an issue with reputable makeup companies who are trying in earnest to reach a more diverse clientele. The darker shades turn red or orange. That, or they wrongly assume deeper skin doesn't have yellow undertones. I have faith LM will either re-formulate or introduce another shade that can be worn for those of us who have dark or deep skin with yellow undertones. In the meantime, I've found wearing a little of this without any foundation makes my natural skin look heavenly--the oxidization isn't noticeable, it stands up against heat and sweat, and my dynamic complexion comes through. So, it turns out I purchased a surprise product I didn't know I wanted."

faceoff_negative: "I own the contour wand by CT, and I love it. I bought this one to try it out. I bought it in the shade cool bronze and it's a good product, except I find myself using a lot of the product to get the intensity I like. Mind you I like it quite natural. I would say CT (light-medium) is pure pigment, you do not need much product to get a nice bronze look. I would choose my CT over Sculpt tape. I won't be returning it, I'm going to keep it because like I said is still a good product. I just wouldn't tell people is a dupe. Definitely get it if you are looking for something light and natural. But if you want something pigmented and effortless try the CT contour wand, I think is worth it."
faceoff_positive: "I for sure was one who was saying this product blends into nothing. I've seen some reviews where they say it dries quickly so only do one area at a time, but when I did that I found the product almost like disappeared (I was using a sponge so that sponge also soaked up a lot of product) So instead I now apply this to all areas of my face I want to bronze/contour, then go to blend it out and I've found that definitely gives more color payout. It can also get deep super fast that way as well, almost like it warms on the skin. Be careful especially if you're planning on using a pigmented powder bronzer on top. I went overboard one day \uD83D\uDE05. I enjoy the squeeze tube with the locking mechanism so this doesn't get squeezed and leak all over the top and my makeup bag. Good amount of product for how little dots you need all over. Remember folks, liquid is DIFFERENT than a cream 100%"
